<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-adasid-04146a65" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-604711a6c316538a">Why isn&#x27;t SID overlap always harmful?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic sharing transfers related information; harmful collisions obstruct discrimination or overload learning. Adapt penalties rather than maximize separation everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Color variants can share coarse clothing semantics while still differing at fine inventory codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-604711a6c316538a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb18b863121823e9">Why not penalize all same-SID pairs equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some overlap is useful semantics, some harmful congestion. AdaSID adapts to load, compatibility, and training phase. Uniform penalties can destroy meaningful sharing or tolerate overloaded collisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar running shoes can share a coarse code; shoes and ovens sharing a crowded code may need stronger correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb18b863121823e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e97e8e859bc568b">What does an adaptive coefficient change compared with fixed collision loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pair and training time affect severity, allowing early semantic organization and later discrimination. Flexibility adds calibration cost and still needs matched evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Related books can share a code early, with high-load distinctions strengthened later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e97e8e859bc568b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6575b5aeeca1f0cc">Is AdaSID&#x27;s collision coefficient a single scalar?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>λij(t) depends on pair load, compatibility, and time. Apply it to the corresponding overlap before summing and report the schedule. A constant removes adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shoes and books can receive different penalties at the same step and change later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6575b5aeeca1f0cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-agent-web-rec-883c9fbf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a24e04c7fcabf5a">What do private memory and neighbor patterns each provide?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Private memory is personal evidence retrieved by meaning and recency. Neighbor patterns supplement weak coverage, without overriding strong direct evidence or becoming facts about the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use the user&#x27;s lightweight-camera preference before asking about an unfamiliar outdoor need.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a24e04c7fcabf5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4633804b5ff7685">Why ask neighboring agents only when private evidence is insufficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Personal relevant memories are primary. Retrieve with semantics and recency; low confidence triggers compact neighbor patterns rather than raw history. Local gate/fusion checks are not full agent capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use repeated vegetarian preferences directly; seek general travel patterns for vague new interest without sharing itineraries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4633804b5ff7685">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0465c8ff0561e985">What is the trade-off versus always aggregating neighbors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Always collaborating may cover more but adds communication and noise. Confidence gating saves calls; overconfidence misses help, underconfidence calls too often. Local results are diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not inject popular gaming patterns into a request with clear photography evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0465c8ff0561e985">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6ad3296c97edfb6">What should time decay and collaboration thresholds test separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep time units consistent and avoid giving future events anomalous gains. Compare confidence κ to its own threshold, separate from retrieval rank. Check sorting, expiry, and trigger boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A top-scoring memory is not automatically sufficient evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6ad3296c97edfb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-akt-rec-be638f5f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-839084f49fa9670e">Why retain cluster and individual views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clusters share knowledge where feedback is scarce; individual embeddings preserve behavior differences. Activity gates balance them and soft orthogonality encourages complementarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two sci-fi films can share a cluster while preserving action versus philosophical audiences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-839084f49fa9670e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-45241ee3447dbb5c">Why teach tail items from head items asymmetrically and stop teacher gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heads have richer interactions. Weight tail-to-head transfer while preventing tail noise from altering teachers. Cluster/individual views and activity gates preserve distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new shoe borrows common knowledge without a few accidental clicks rewriting the best-selling cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45241ee3447dbb5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5233252aac6658c3">Does asymmetric transfer just add more contrastive examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It weights tail-to-head learning and detaches teacher-side gradients, unlike symmetric adjustment. This assumes heads are more reliable and may fail in some clusters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new niche film can learn from established neighbors without pulling them toward its noisy clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5233252aac6658c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-904bf22dbb99d023">Where are AKT-Rec&#x27;s two activity gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First blend cluster and individual item embeddings; second blend cluster and instance histories based on user/item/cross activity. Do not collapse them or detach both contrastive sides.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new item can need cluster embeddings and a sparse user can independently need cluster history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-904bf22dbb99d023">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-atomic-intent-04e8fc99" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-39f0b65e8c995c63">Why does Atomic Intent break an action into a hierarchy of intents rather than assigning one broad category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A category records what the user viewed; hierarchical intents also attempt to describe purpose and need, so cross-domain behavior can connect through shared intents. Offline extraction preserves fine-grained cacheable units, and the online target item retrieves relevant chains. An inferred intent can be wrong and is not an explicit user statement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camera browsing could reflect a need for light travel gear or studio image quality. A generic photography label loses the distinction between evidence for a lightweight bag and for studio lighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39f0b65e8c995c63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc84ca215cad39e2">Why isn&#x27;t cached atomic intent equivalent to one user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchical retrievable evidence lets each target select an intent chain. Expensive reasoning happens offline; candidate retrieval/fusion stays online. Local proxy does not verify full LLM intent generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve camping for a tent and lightweight-equipment needs for a commuting bag from the same memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc84ca215cad39e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4a523cd28e8acb5">How does target-conditioned retrieval in Atomic Intent differ from a static text profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A static summary compresses needs into one account seen by every candidate. Atomic chains are indexed individually, support incremental updates, and let candidates fetch different evidence. Offline parsing, storage, and retrieval need maintenance; aggregation cannot recover evidence omitted by the index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shoes can retrieve exercise needs while cameras retrieve travel photography needs. A fixed summary that only says the user likes the outdoors loses both specific reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4a523cd28e8acb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa74ccdb0259971a">Why validate Atomic Intent&#x27;s intent extraction and online aggregation separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-frequency and time decay weight evidence; they do not replace offline LLM extraction of hierarchical intent. Similarity retrieval and multi-head aggregation should consume cached chains. If the local implementation only has deterministic proxy scores, a runnable formula does not establish that it reproduces the LLM extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weighting ten views by age produces a number, not an explanation such as traveling light. Check the cache first, then the online selection to locate the two kinds of error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa74ccdb0259971a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:bahe" data-paper-title="Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-bahe-7645b8ec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3738cc4f91a5ce4c">Why is BAHE&#x27;s atomic behavior cache different from caching the final user representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abahe">Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An atomic cache holds shallow single-item content encodings reusable across histories. The final user representation also depends on order, the current candidate, and higher-layer interactions. Asynchronous shallow updates remove repeated text work; the upper layer still learns personalized combinations. Finer caching increases reuse but requires version consistency and care over compression losses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two users can read the same cached title vector in different history orders without sharing final interest scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.19347-bahe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3738cc4f91a5ce4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:bahe" data-paper-title="Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e6d87b8ce07426e">Why does BAHE still train higher-layer aggregation when shallow encodings of atomic behavior are cached?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abahe">Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shallow layers encode reusable text semantics for individual actions; higher layers need the current history and candidate and cannot be frozen into a universal answer. This moves repeated text computation off training and request paths while retaining interactions. Stale or excessively compressed cache entries can harm quality despite better efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cache a movie title once, but aggregate it differently when watched alongside science fiction or family movies and when scoring different candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.19347-bahe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e6d87b8ce07426e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:bahe" data-paper-title="Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cdffe7e92c04133d">Where does BAHE save computation compared with rerunning the full text model per sample, and what can it lose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abahe">Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated shallow encoding is avoided, and upper layers process actions rather than every word token. Compression removes detail and changes capacity, so measure time and quality together. Local time fell but AUC also fell, supporting the efficiency mechanism rather than a quality-preserving substitution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten titles may contain over a hundred words; ten cached behavior vectors are quicker to process, but losing a critical phrase can damage ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.19347-bahe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cdffe7e92c04133d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:bahe" data-paper-title="Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1dad8a6e15629cc">How does the local two-layer BERT-tiny BAHE split caching and training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abahe">Breaking the Length Barrier: LLM-Enhanced CTR Prediction in Long Textual User Behaviors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The first layer generates and caches atomic MovieLens title vectors. The copied upper layer processes CLS, 12 history entries, and the candidate. The control runs frozen lower and trainable upper layers per sample with matched data and budget. Bind the cache to the shallow version; a two-layer timing ratio does not predict production-scale gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the upper layer expects a different shallow encoder version from the cache producer, vector semantics can mismatch. Record the vector and upper-layer versions together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19347">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.19347-bahe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1dad8a6e15629cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:camie" data-paper-title="CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-camie-634faffd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5287e4bcfb9cffed">Why should one CAMIE checkpoint support image-text and text-only products?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acamie">CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real catalog modality availability varies. A shared interface lets products without pictures enter the same retrieval space instead of requiring separate models. Joint training and behavior alignment support matching across inputs, but a missing image removes information, so accuracy need not be equal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A title-only launch and an item with images and attributes can both be indexed, but the former has no visual details to recover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.30255-camie/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5287e4bcfb9cffed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:camie" data-paper-title="CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b92b9cd74adef7f">Why add co-engagement contrastive learning rather than training CAMIE item vectors only on image-text similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acamie">CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content resemblance does not guarantee a consumption relationship. CAMIE uses item pairs jointly engaged with in a user journey for symmetric contrastive supervision, shaping multimodal embeddings for recommendation. The shared encoder supports variable modality availability. Co-engagement still reflects exposure and context, not universal complementarity or causal demand.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar furniture can serve incompatible uses, while visually different desks and chairs are often considered together. Behavior supervision adds that relation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.30255-camie/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b92b9cd74adef7f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:camie" data-paper-title="CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76fca7b0a2ff4204">How do CAMIE&#x27;s co-engagement positives differ from generic image-text contrastive positives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acamie">CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Image-text positives typically pair modalities of the same content. Co-engagement pairs different items that share user interactions in a journey, encoding potential complementarity or sequential needs. Exposure still affects which items co-occur, so it is not an unbiased complementarity label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tent and sleeping bag may convert together despite very different images; two popular items may merely co-occur because both receive heavy exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.30255-camie/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76fca7b0a2ff4204">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:camie" data-paper-title="CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-74acf9ceaf1f9727">Why compute both directions of CAMIE&#x27;s symmetric in-batch InfoNCE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acamie">CAMIE: Co-Engagement-Aware Multimodal Item Embeddings for Snap Dynamic Product Ads Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One direction uses a as query and its paired b as positive among the batch&#x27;s b values. Swap sides to supervise both encoders and average the losses. Pairs must share the intended journey relation, temperature controls sharpness, and duplicated positives should not blindly count as negatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn camera-to-lens and lens-to-camera matching. A duplicate row for the same positive lens would otherwise give contradictory supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.30255-camie/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74acf9ceaf1f9727">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-connectionmind-47def159" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efd96cc24e42c304">Why output graph evidence paths instead of only a social recommendation score in ConnectionMind?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A path shows which user, item, and semantic relations support the recommendation, enabling checks of edges, timestamps, and weights and supervision at each step. It is an explicit trajectory, not a fabricated explanation. Legality does not guarantee recommendation utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Show the graph edges from a friend&#x27;s photography collection to a tutorial. A claim that friends might like it is not equivalent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efd96cc24e42c304">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ac4878088ac5aa1">Why does ConnectionMind produce evidence paths and distill its path teacher into a GNN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paths expose intermediate graph relations and support step-level supervision and rewards. An LLM searches heterogeneous subgraphs for complex requests, while a distilled student handles ordinary traffic at lower cost. Paths must come from the visible graph; training shortest positive paths cannot be supplied as evaluation answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A path through a followed creator and photography topic to a tutorial is inspectable. The student can reuse the relation pattern without full LLM search for every request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ac4878088ac5aa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c016e4a2ff19e166">How does ConnectionMind&#x27;s stepwise policy compare with fixed GNN aggregation in scope and serving cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy selects task-dependent frontier expansions and relation paths; a GNN aggregates over fixed propagation structure. Full search is more flexible and expensive, so only complex minority traffic uses it. Locally, perfect path legality coexisted with negative recommendation results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Complex requests can explore friends and shared tags, while ordinary ones use a distilled model. Legal steps can still lead mostly to overly popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c016e4a2ff19e166">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a25300cbe57ccb6c">When can ConnectionMind&#x27;s shortest-path demonstrations use target answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can derive step supervision from positive targets. Evaluation searches only the visible graph and current context, without held-out targets or gold paths. Keep format, recommendation, and path-shaping rewards distinct. Giving the agent a test answer path is diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Showing how to navigate to a known item teaches training; revealing the correct movie node before test search cannot establish recommendation capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a25300cbe57ccb6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cross-domain-kd-40631210" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcb82583790cb527">Why can cross-domain KD run a source teacher on target examples without source logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher output distributions and auxiliary signals carry knowledge without replaying source training data. Target labels constrain the real serving task and the teacher must understand available target features. Removing data access does not verify new-domain calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A video teacher provides soft preferences to a music student without sharing video logs; some video preferences may not transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcb82583790cb527">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9d9d3587756f447">Why can cross-domain distillation omit source training data but not blindly trust the source teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher can provide task and auxiliary signals directly on target examples, so raw source logs are unnecessary. The teacher may still be miscalibrated or lack important new-domain features. Use target supervision, and do not hide negative local comparisons behind teacher size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Video-domain preferences can inform music, but equating video viewing habits with music listening can transfer errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9d9d3587756f447">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d39e67ee64576bf2">What do target-only student and same-domain DIN controls test in cross-domain KD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target-only comparison isolates added distillation knowledge; DIN anchors overall model quality. Internal gains do not mean matching a stronger baseline, and the source reports very different results under the two controls. A temperature ablation cannot replace matched data, candidates, and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student improving from 10 to 11 is an internal gain, but does not beat a DIN score of 30.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d39e67ee64576bf2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c569ebb41759c020">Why does temperature distillation use `T²`, and how should auxiliary logits align in cross-domain KD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Temperature changes softmax sharpness and gradient scale; `T²` compensates for the latter. Teacher and student tasks and classes must correspond semantically, not merely by shape. Serving only needs the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher long-watch head should not be matched to a student payment head. Higher temperature cannot fix a task mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c569ebb41759c020">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dme-01722658" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de44944ba6c76358">Why does DME use cross-conditioned reconstruction as well as contrastive learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrastive supervision tells embeddings which examples should be near but can lose distinctions. Reconstructing document details from queries and query details from documents encourages compressed embeddings to keep useful semantics, not lossless reconstruction or extra serving information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two camping documents share a theme but differ in winter warmth versus light weight; reconstruction encourages preserving that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de44944ba6c76358">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-602408aa518e2b96">Why are DME&#x27;s reasoning and reconstruction heads used only during training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrastive retrieval can lose fine-grained evidence. Typed latent targets and cross-reconstruction push embeddings to retain relevant information about the other side. Serving uses efficient similarity without per-pair reasoning text; auxiliary losses do not guarantee faithful explainability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teach query vectors to retain relevant material and use cases, then serve nearest-neighbor retrieval without generating explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-602408aa518e2b96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a00832a5e933a66e">What does DME typed latent evidence retain or give up compared with online chain of thought?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structured internal evidence trains embeddings while serving stays vector-based. Online CoT provides readable steps at extra latency. DME trades that textual explanation for retrieval efficiency, and latent evidence does not establish faithful chains. Local reconstruction proxies are not full multimodal heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with place and purpose evidence types but serve retrieval only, without claiming the system generated a stepwise rationale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a00832a5e933a66e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c41913d999f5f16">Why verify that DME&#x27;s generation heads are removed from serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both heads provide training supervision only. Running reconstruction online violates intended latency and dependencies; never training the heads does not establish reconstruction learning. The local ridge diagnostic is distinct from the paper&#x27;s large multimodal heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log both reconstruction losses and export only the two encoders. Turning heads on for quality and off for latency would evaluate different models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c41913d999f5f16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dos-16f0eac2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0437ee0944985852">Why do DOS behavior and semantic streams shape one codebook together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction alone can miss collaborative distinctions. Behavior provides consumption relations and content preserves semantic structure. Balance both to avoid popularity overwhelming details; co-occurrence is not semantic identity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar-topic movies with different audiences can separate, while different genres sharing travel interests may gain useful links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0437ee0944985852">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74c3aabfa7722897">Why does DOS orthogonally rotate content vectors before residual quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Original directions can concentrate information in a few coordinates. Rotation redistributes directions while preserving geometry; residual quantization allocates coarse and fine information, with both behavior and content calibrating the codebook. Orthogonality does not make semantics independent or prove recommendation utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotation can spread concentrated coordinate variance, but only behavioral targets show whether it separates attributes users care about.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74c3aabfa7722897">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-639f0d81779c4784">Why constrain DOS projection to be orthogonal rather than freely learned?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Orthogonal transforms preserve distances and norms while reorienting the space for quantization. General projections can distort scales. Constraints reduce freedom but do not minimize quantization error or ensure independent semantic factors. The local Procrustes path is a specific controlled version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating axes preserves pairwise distance, unlike stretching an axis, but a better grid orientation does not causally decompose preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-639f0d81779c4784">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-23e5ceb782b20c24">Why check both orthogonality and reconstruction errors in DOS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>`WᵀW` near identity verifies rotation only. Reconstruction checks residual-code approximation; good values on both still do not prove retrieval quality. Use the same rotation version for training and evaluation and document mapping changes before reusing codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A perfectly orthogonal W may align points poorly with the codebook, so near-zero orthogonality error cannot replace reconstruction or ranking scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23e5ceb782b20c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dual-sid-924ced9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-46865ea59a025071">Why should a Dual-purpose SID code also reconstruct a content vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It supports both generative nomination and ranking features. SiDec converts small indices into approximate content, reducing per-item storage and transmission while training the codes not to retain only collaborative identity. Measure quality loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small codes save bandwidth but cannot reconstruct a waterproofing property they never encoded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
