<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-46865ea59a025071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f49a93e9e5190c4">Why does Dual-purpose SID use SiDec to reconstruct content embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An identity code alone may not supply the high-dimensional content needed downstream. SiDec reconstructs content from short codes for lower I/O while preserving discrete recommendation identity. Compression is lossy, and local small-codebook quality loss must be reported separately from bandwidth gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three short codes can replace a large vector read, but a decoder cannot recover differences between products that collide in their codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f49a93e9e5190c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5608c346f04ecf0b">What is the resource trade-off between short SID plus SiDec and a cached dense embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense caches preserve vectors at storage and I/O cost. Short codes shift per-item storage into indices and shared decoding, adding compute and error. Lower I/O is not necessarily lower end-to-end latency, and a small-codebook retrieval regression remains meaningful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A million vectors can become codes, but a decoding matrix on each request may be costly and a small codebook can hurt relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5608c346f04ecf0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c88c2829edde23f">Why concatenate separate one-hot columns per code level in SiDec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical integers denote different residual-layer codewords. Layer offsets preserve identity before decoding to content width. Keep item and version aligned with reconstruction targets; the local ridge decoder is a scaled-down path, not full reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code 3 at level one and code 3 at level two require different input columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c88c2829edde23f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dynamic-codebook-fbc8657c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc885da512bc2b5b">Why is a one-stage large codebook shorter to decode but not equivalent to a unique item ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One level shortens the path, but finite centers may each represent multiple items. Separate collision codes give uniqueness. A large vocabulary increases candidate and update costs, so fewer steps alone do not establish overall savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short book code can identify a bucket shared by two books; it cannot specify the display item without disambiguation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc885da512bc2b5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-378a7edc8250a731">Why does a large one-stage dynamic codebook still need collision codes and exposure-weighted updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer semantic steps reduce autoregressive work, but shared codes need extra disambiguation. Exposure-weighted updates adapt center resolution to real usage and change index semantics, so generation and serving mappings must stay synchronized.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The main code identifies a popular group and a collision code identifies the item. Reading an obsolete mapping can return the wrong item despite faster decoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-378a7edc8250a731">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-335cd5a8867b9d57">How do dynamic and frozen codebooks trade distribution adaptation against path stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen centers preserve meaning. Updates adapt to new content and exposure but may misalign older generators and indexes. Exposure weights can reinforce policy bias; measure update benefits, drift, and version maintenance separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Holiday arrivals can justify moving centers, but old items changing code silently would make the generator&#x27;s old probabilities wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335cd5a8867b9d57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-84a3e3fd94a94437">Why define an explicit empty-bucket rule for weighted codebook updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A weighted mean with zero total weight is undefined. Retain or handle empty centers under a defined rule rather than random fallback after division by zero. Publish EMA centers, assignments, and collision mappings in one version and disclose changes to the algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Without any item entering code 7, there is no evidence for a new center; arbitrary reset invalidates existing paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84a3e3fd94a94437">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-filterllm-8613b323" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efbde829d9a93e90">Why predict audiences rather than next items from new product text in FilterLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cold-start items have little interaction, so the task is to find likely users proactively. One encoding yields a compressed audience distribution mapped back to people. Scores are modeled inclinations, not observed reactions or explicit rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate interest among camping and travel audiences for a new tent without a billion individual LLM calls, then collect real feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efbde829d9a93e90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-00503df2eae5a2ba">Why does FilterLLM predict an audience distribution from item text rather than asking an LLM about each user?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pairwise decisions scale with audience size and are costly for new items. Encode the item once and predict probabilities over a compressed user vocabulary supervised by historical behavior. Compression trades sharing for resolution; group probabilities are not reliable personalized judgments for each member.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict an audience distribution once for a new article instead of generating one LLM answer per user, while accepting loss of individual detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00503df2eae5a2ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d3a5310eb724f26">How does a compressed user vocabulary trade output size against personalization versus per-user classification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clustering users produces a smaller distribution covering many individuals but loses within-group detail and changes with data and grouping. The local genre-text proxy regressed, so scalability alone is not cold-start quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A highly scored beginner photography group includes someone who just bought a camera and may not need another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d3a5310eb724f26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a43ab96f505a54aa">Why not equate nonexposure with dislike in FilterLLM target distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observed interactions reflect exposure. Specify `q(u|i)` normalization, vocabulary mapping, and training cutoff; test interactions cannot build targets. Otherwise the model copies prior exposure or leaks future evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user who never saw a tent might like camping; forcing zero for all unexposed users prevents finding new audiences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a43ab96f505a54aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:finesid" data-paper-title="Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-finesid-1b73a633" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9710414fc4bd3e4">Why keep fine-grained visual and text tokens rather than a single product code in FineSID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afinesid">Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single code can discard local texture, regions, and text details that drive relevance and clicks. Discrete local tokens support richer interactions through relevance pretraining but cost more in training and serving. More granularity does not guarantee better recommendations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two coats differ mainly in cuffs or pockets; a single summary code may lose the deciding detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 三阶段结构, 成本判定：不执行复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9710414fc4bd3e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:finesid" data-paper-title="Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f378d3166750e8f2">Why does FineSID need more than SID embeddings when transferring relevance pretraining to CTR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afinesid">Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevance pretraining teaches ordered content fusion and HiFormer interactions across embeddings, dense layers, and normalization state. Copying only the vocabulary loses much of that learning. Change the CTR head and handle optimizer state explicitly. Full experiments were excluded for cost; random-token fixtures are not substitutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Copying codes without the layers that match query uses to image details transfers a dictionary but not how to read it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 三阶段结构, 成本判定：不执行复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f378d3166750e8f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:finesid" data-paper-title="Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a81772613dcdad3d">How does full FineSID predictor transfer differ from freezing a content encoder and adding a CTR head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afinesid">Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen encoder mainly transfers content features; FineSID also retains cross-token fusion, interaction networks, and state learned on relevance, then adapts to personalized CTR. This costs more and requires matched interfaces. The repository completed cost review, not a reduced-model performance run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Transfer the matching network that relates query conditions to item details, not just a content vocabulary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 三阶段结构, 成本判定：不执行复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a81772613dcdad3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:finesid" data-paper-title="Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f9ddee4a7682fef">Why explicitly handle optimizer and normalization state at FineSID stage transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afinesid">Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full transfer includes interaction layers and normalization statistics beyond SID embeddings. Keeping or resetting optimizer state changes training dynamics and must follow the stage contract, as must conversion to the CTR head. These requirements are documented; no local training validates performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Copying weights without their normalization can change scale abruptly, and old task momentum should not silently enter a new CTR head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 三阶段结构, 成本判定：不执行复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f9ddee4a7682fef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fluid" data-paper-title="FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-fluid-d95a4248" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a48a51ad5530b68f">Why treat live slices and room-history summaries as distinct tokens in FLUID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afluid">FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok / ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The slice LUCID reflects fast-changing current content while the room LUCID aggregates stable historical semantics. Late fusion prevents historical majority from erasing fresh themes. A room vote can miss minority changes and cannot replace the slice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A beauty creator currently discussing travel storage has different room and slice signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21832">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21832-fluid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a48a51ad5530b68f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fluid" data-paper-title="FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0acb1d4423aebec">Why does FLUID keep slice and room LUCIDs and phase out item IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afluid">FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok / ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short-lived rooms accumulate little stable ID feedback. Slice codes describe current content and room codes aggregate stable history. Late fusion keeps the time scales distinct; add slices, remove IDs, then add rooms to ease training transitions. Content codes can still collide or go stale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sportswear room may currently sell shoes; room and slice codes describe different evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21832">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21832-fluid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0acb1d4423aebec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fluid" data-paper-title="FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-66592890548a71b4">What shared information does FLUID use after removing transient item IDs instead of randomly initializing new room IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afluid">FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok / ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random IDs learn only after interactions. Semantic prefixes reuse cross-domain content patterns immediately, useful for short-lived rooms, but lose distinct identity memory. Removing IDs lowered overall local quality; report that alongside improved freshness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A ten-minute stream has little time to train an ID. Content can place it immediately but may not distinguish hosting styles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21832">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21832-fluid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66592890548a71b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fluid" data-paper-title="FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ddf0ab5507e099e9">Why index each LUCID embedding by the full prefix rather than an isolated codeword?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afluid">FLUID: From Ephemeral IDs to Multimodal Semantic Codes for Industrial-Scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok / ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A later code depends on earlier residual choices; cumulative prefix indexes retain path identity. Isolated codewords merge different branches. Final candidate tokens must contain only room and slice codes to implement item-ID removal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fine code 3 after beauty and after travel needs separate embedding entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21832">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.21832-fluid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ddf0ab5507e099e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-g2rec-310e6cb6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-32417801d1e00372">Why insert interest-profile tokens between G2Rec item tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item tokens preserve identity; profiles expose shared graph-based interests from multiple memberships. Alternating tokens lets generation use both. Profiles are model structure, not extra consumed events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A travel photography book can carry both interests through an adjacent mixed profile instead of its ID alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32417801d1e00372">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-262f93f892309abd">Why allow each G2Rec item to belong softly to multiple interest prototypes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same item can serve several audiences, and hard assignment loses cross-interest relations. Learn soft memberships from the global co-engagement graph and alternate prototype-combined interest tokens with items. Build the graph only from visible training behavior to prevent leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camping cooking video can contribute to outdoor and cooking prototypes without forcing either audience into one label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-262f93f892309abd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54e73b36a95c0b86">How does G2Rec soft modularity form interest groups differently from a fixed taxonomy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Taxonomy imposes buckets. Soft modularity learns overlapping communities from co-engagement while accounting for degree background. Communities need not match human categories and can reflect exposure. Graph quality does not guarantee sequence ranking improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camera and travel bag can share a community while one book partially belongs to a second one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54e73b36a95c0b86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0bb6b1185f0a09e">What should be checked in G2Rec&#x27;s prototype means and alternating sequences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight item vectors by membership and divide by total weight with explicit handling for empty or tiny clusters. Align item/profile positions and causal masks; auxiliary targets cannot read future items. Local evaluation uses one positive and 99 negatives, not full-catalog ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Item A must be followed by A&#x27;s profile, not B&#x27;s, even if a misaligned sequence still reduces loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0bb6b1185f0a09e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gala-83e5be9a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bc4828f01afa008">Why are GALA multimodal and ID representations complementary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content transfers semantics and IDs retain platform behavior history. A contextual gate chooses their contributions, and behavior rewards align pretrained semantics to recommendation. Neither replaces the other universally, particularly with new items lacking feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new product relies on image/text use cues, whereas a popular older one has rich click history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bc4828f01afa008">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a98952ce877a50dd">Why does GALA use behavior rewards and gated ID fusion after image-text pretraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content alignment does not ensure personalized consumption relevance. Behavior rewards adapt multimodal representations, while a gate balances semantic and collaborative ID evidence per example, including cold starts. Biased rewards or a collapsed gate can fail; multimodal retrieval is not final recommendation value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching product images and copy do not make a product right for this user; established and new items can rely on different evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a98952ce877a50dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b1a61d045c96205">How does GALA&#x27;s behavioral GRPO differ from image-text pretraining in supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pretraining aligns queries, images, and text. Behavior-driven post-training compares options under actual recommendation targets rather than content similarity alone. Exposure bias and loss of semantic capability remain possible; a public proxy does not establish full policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually similar coats can perform differently for commuter users; behavioral alignment can capture that beyond correct image-text pairing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b1a61d045c96205">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b28d03f4103a30f">Why align dimensions and item identity before applying GALA&#x27;s sigmoid gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Elementwise gates need equal-width multimodal and ID vectors for the same candidate, and their inputs must match that pair. Bounded sigmoid values cannot repair mismatches; handle missing cold-start IDs explicitly and distinguish local proxies from full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mixing item A&#x27;s image/text vector with item B&#x27;s ID can yield finite values without representing either item correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b28d03f4103a30f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gatesid-592868f0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e3b073964f33ff7">Why use cold-start degree to set semantic and collaborative proportions in GateSID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content shares knowledge when collaborative feedback is scarce; mature ID behavior should preserve distinctions. A state-conditioned gate avoids one ratio across items but activity is not the only reliability signal and can mislead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new running shoe borrows content, while an established one keeps audience-specific behavior despite similar descriptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e3b073964f33ff7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e115da7ec1187834">Why does GateSID let cold-start degree control semantic–collaborative fusion and alignment strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse feedback makes collaborative vectors noisy, so strong alignment can corrupt content. Rich feedback contains distinctions that content averaging may erase. Condition both fusion and alignment on evidence strength, adapting as interactions arrive instead of assigning all new items permanently to content only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two textually similar items differ because one has strong audience feedback while the other just launched; a fixed 50:50 mix ignores that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e115da7ec1187834">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea48736e0ac71216">How does gating alignment strength in GateSID differ from mixing final scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final blending only changes use of existing representations. Training-time alignment changes how closely the spaces are learned together. Strong alignment can propagate noisy evidence, so conditional gating limits it; the mechanism does not prove gains in all cold-start slices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lowering a new item&#x27;s ID score at the end may not undo semantic corruption caused by forcing early alignment to a noisy ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea48736e0ac71216">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-62b81621b4bfe67a">Why must GateSID&#x27;s cold-start features use only pre-cutoff data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts and activity set the gate. Test-future interactions reveal later maturity and corrupt the cold-start scenario. Align dimensions before fusion and use real per-example adaptation rather than calling a fixed validation constant adaptive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item that goes viral during test cannot use the week&#x27;s final click count for an earlier recommendation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62b81621b4bfe67a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gris-e106351a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ea41541f1d110b0">Why formulate GrIS SID construction as hierarchical graph partitioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nodes supply content and edges supply collaborative consumption relations. Recursive partitioning creates coarse-to-fine paths beyond content reconstruction. Exposure and popularity affect graph structure, so hierarchy is not a guaranteed true taxonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cameras and lenses can share a high-level interest region through co-consumption and separate into lower-level content groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ea41541f1d110b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-362f60f3895a3566">Why does GrIS use both item features and collaborative edges to construct SIDs by graph partitioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content proximity and co-consumption differ. Hierarchical partitions balance semantic features and collaborative links; without graph evidence fall back to content rather than inventing edges. Local partition and state checks do not verify generative or online recommendation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Co-consumed camping gear can connect despite visual differences; new items without edges must mainly use content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-362f60f3895a3566">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4acebc44815e676c">How does GrIS&#x27;s content fallback for an empty graph differ from inventing adjacency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fallback openly uses only available content and gives a defined control. Synthetic edges presented as observations change the objective. Report graph availability and do not infer large-scale ranking from diagnostics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new product can use title semantics, not fabricated links to popular items claimed as collaborative evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4acebc44815e676c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b80b3cbd72b4d963">Why save node identities and parent paths at each GrIS recursive split?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Refinement stays inside each current subgraph. Without parent paths, local child IDs from distinct branches can collide. Implement smoothing, semantic combination, and empty-graph handling explicitly; integer outputs alone do not verify content-and-collaboration hierarchy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two parent clusters can each have child 2, but their full SIDs must differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b80b3cbd72b4d963">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-idproxy-2c030d0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e485c22823c9b5a">Why is an IDProxy proxy not just the original MLLM embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The MLLM learns content semantics, whereas ranking IDs capture collaborative behavior; their directions and scales can differ. After coarse alignment and multilayer adaptation, a gated proxy increment supplements the original ID representation. A concatenation that happens to run is not evidence of successful space adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Similar-looking products can have distinct audiences that raw content embeddings miss but ID history preserves. The proxy should add information without replacing that distinction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e485c22823c9b5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-94883dce7d68b562">Why does IDProxy align the MLLM and ID spaces before injecting multilayer proxy residuals into a ranker?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multimodal semantics describe content but need not match the collaborative coordinates learned from long-term CTR training. Replacing IDs outright can destroy that geometry. Coarse contrastive alignment establishes a correspondence, then multilayer proxies extract knowledge at different abstraction levels and a gate controls its contribution. A residual protects the original path, but controlled comparisons still matter: overly strong semantics can swamp useful collaborative distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two visually similar products may have different audiences, so semantics cannot simply override ID preferences. First align the spaces, then borrow attributes such as shape or use at appropriate levels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94883dce7d68b562">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2785150af7e1a5e">What fallback does IDProxy&#x27;s residual gate preserve relative to completely replacing item IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replacement discards existing collaborative memory; the gate adds adapted semantics on top of the original ID and can limit an unreliable increment. It can still favor one side too much, so check cold and tail items separately from head items. A lower contrastive pretraining loss does not guarantee better ranking; the source supports only its small public protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An established item with abundant feedback may need little semantic input. A new item with a weak ID can borrow more content, but a gate cannot guarantee detection of every content error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2785150af7e1a5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0fdf676b20910cb9">Why must IDProxy construct coarse-alignment pairs using the same item identity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PAL brings an MLLM vector zi near its corresponding ID vector ei, with other IDs in the batch contributing to the denominator. Misaligned columns force unrelated items together. The residual adapter must project to the original ID dimension before addition, and the gate must belong to that candidate. Collect multilayer hidden states from the actual model version rather than substituting random vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camera content paired with a children&#x27;s clothing ID can still reduce training loss while learning the wrong mapping. Matching shapes and plausible values cannot replace identity checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0fdf676b20910cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kar-c442fbbf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b495bedf4e8e1f2">Why separate user preference knowledge and item facts in KAR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A preference explains why a user might like something, while a fact describes what it is; evidence and update frequencies differ. Factorization prompting generates them separately, and the hybrid-expert adapter injects them into the ID recommender rather than conflating facts and guesses in one text. Generated knowledge can still hallucinate and is not observed ground truth.</p>
