<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Enjoying light plots is an inferred preference; a film&#x27;s release year is factual. Writing the preference as an item attribute can contaminate matching and explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b495bedf4e8e1f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-78a75af0fdb7fbca">Why does KAR generate user preference knowledge separately from item facts before applying a hybrid-expert adapter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User knowledge describes why someone might like an item; item knowledge describes the item&#x27;s attributes. Their sources and meanings differ, so plain concatenation may not fit an ID model. Shared and specialized experts compress and align the knowledge for prediction with the original representations. Offline caching avoids online autoregressive generation, but LLM inferences can be wrong and are not user statements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Waterproof material is an item fact; frequently viewing rainy-day hiking content suggests a user preference. An adapter can match them without claiming the user explicitly wants those shoes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78a75af0fdb7fbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-804816a74c553ef3">How do cost and error propagation differ between KAR&#x27;s offline knowledge enhancement and online LLM recommendation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline generation reuses a cache, so serving runs only the adapter and original recommender without autoregressive latency. Mistakes are also reused, making versions and refreshes important. Online generation is more flexible but incurs a cost on every request. The twenty-user reduction in the source shows only a small trend, not general industrial gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One cached film fact can serve many users, but an incorrect year propagates until refreshed. Asking on each request can update it at the cost of extra latency and inconsistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-804816a74c553ef3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fccb1acc024f0dc4">Why validate KAR&#x27;s four-expert gate together with the original ID representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The gate mixes knowledge vectors from shared and specialized experts, then the result is scored with user and item IDs. Dimensions, identities, and gradient flow must agree. Pre-generating a knowledge file does not prove the ranker learned to use it. Cache only from training-visible behavior so preferences do not absorb test answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A ranker can output scores while never reading the knowledge on disk, but that is not KAR. Summarizing user preferences after seeing test behavior instead leaks the target into evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fccb1acc024f0dc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kgd-b25439a8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-28611cd58dfcd19a">Why does KGD&#x27;s BMTP select related future items rather than supervise all adjacent clicks equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adjacent events can be accidental or express different needs; predicting them blindly encodes unhelpful transitions. BMTP selects more meaningful future targets by collaborative or semantic relations and later exposes the knowledge as read-only. Bad relations can miss real emerging interests, and future labels remain training supervision only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An accidental sports-news click after camera browsing need not define a strong transition. A related future lens looks more like the same need, but that is not a reason to exclude all cross-topic exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28611cd58dfcd19a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9bfc27b1d0a91a3">Why does KGD select related future items and make the transfer residual orthogonal to the knowledge anchor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An immediately adjacent click can be noise or a task switch. BMTP picks collaboratively or semantically related future targets to focus pretraining. During transfer, the refreshable knowledge encoder is frozen for the task to read; the residual removes its projection onto the anchor to add new geometry without directly overwriting learned knowledge. Orthogonality constrains direction, not lossless coexistence of all task information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An adjacent accidental click should not provide the same supervision as a persistent photography interest. A new task can try to add price sensitivity outside that anchor rather than rewriting the existing photography semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9bfc27b1d0a91a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0265ca8ff93aafab">What kind of overwrite does KGD&#x27;s orthogonal ACR restrict relative to an ordinary residual adapter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ACR removes the residual projection along the knowledge anchor to avoid directly changing the existing main direction. An ordinary residual can add in any direction, increasing flexibility and the risk of interference. Orthogonality is a geometric constraint, not proof that knowledge is unchanged or semantics independent. Verify effects by task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the anchor already points toward photography, an adapter can add budget distinctions instead of only amplifying that direction. A perpendicular vector could still contain noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0265ca8ff93aafab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c165c1f6afe4f688">How should KGD verify gradient flow and zero-norm handling for read-only knowledge and orthogonal projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the knowledge encoder or explicitly version its refreshes; task loss must not update it through the read-only interface. ACR&#x27;s projection denominator depends on anchor norm, so define handling for zero or near-zero anchors. Merely subtracting r−e is not orthogonal projection. The bounded local mechanism does not reproduce full streaming production transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A zero anchor has no direction, so division by its norm is invalid. If knowledge parameters change after backward, the transfer is not read-only even if output shapes look right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c165c1f6afe4f688">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kuafu-25c887d3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0262d391f69475fd">Why does KuaFu compress both memory token count and channel dimension?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A behavior first has a high-dimensional memory representation, then is projected into fewer, lower-dimensional cached vectors. This saves sequence positions and storage bandwidth separately, and the decoder composes entries in sequence order. Two-axis compression can lose information; reconstructing some answers is not evidence of preserving every temporal or causal relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compressing a 24-word event into two low-dimensional vectors saves more storage than merely halving the word count, but names or times may disappear. Measure that with task metrics, not compression rate alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0262d391f69475fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfd1f5565460f95f">Why compress and cache individual behaviors in KuaFu rather than compressing a user&#x27;s entire history into one vector first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Individual behavior encodings can be reused across users or profiling tasks, and a new event needs only its cache entry. Compressing the whole history binds shared content to user context and can force recomputation on every change. The decoder reads compressed events chronologically and can compose them. Compression loses information, and cache efficiency must not hide the negative local diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Several users can reuse the encoding of the same video behavior. When one watches another video, append its cached representation and decode in order rather than re-encoding all old text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfd1f5565460f95f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-27c383a0aff67bc2">Why do KuaFu&#x27;s input ablation and independently trained raw-text baseline have different evidentiary strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Switching a decoder trained on compressed inputs to raw text confounds the comparison with adaptation to the input distribution. Training the same model separately under the raw-text budget better compares the training paths. The source remained negative after the independent control, and the comparison was not formal equal-FLOPs evaluation, so do not report compression efficiency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A decoder trained only on compressed codes might struggle with truncated text because it is unfamiliar. Training the raw-text branch independently reduces that confound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27c383a0aff67bc2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-766156687183b855">Why should KuaFu report skipped_zero_advantage when every reward in the RL smoke test is equal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical group rewards yield no relative advantage and no usable policy-gradient signal. Invoking the optimizer does not mean RL succeeded. The source preserves the skipped update and verifies QA compression training separately from RL. A GPU forward pass does not prove successful reward optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four answers each score one, so their normalized advantages are zero. The model cannot prefer any answer from that signal; report no update instead of calling the four high rewards learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-766156687183b855">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-l2rec-4fe523da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1acdc921702b9a6f">Why distinguish semantic and behavioral LoRA experts in L2Rec&#x27;s shared LLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text meaning differs from collaborative consumption. View-specific low-rank updates, user routing, and cross-view gating preserve a common backbone alongside distinct task geometries. Experts are shared, not independent models for each user, and personalization depends on routing and data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A semantic expert understands suspense; a behavioral expert captures that group&#x27;s consumption habits. They need not point in the same direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1acdc921702b9a6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f9d51153d32097b">Why does L2Rec use separate user-routed LoRA experts for semantic and behavioral views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content and collaborative behavior can complement or contradict each other. Sharing all adapter parameters can let the stronger signal overwhelm the other. The experts learn view-specific low-rank directions, user routing picks mixtures, and a cross-view gate fuses them. Parameter efficiency still needs supervision, and a router that always selects the same expert defeats specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Content can help a new user; rich co-consumption may matter more for an established user. Separate views can adapt before being combined per user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f9d51153d32097b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d206ae586f50093">How does user-routed LoRA-MoE change parameter sharing compared with one global LoRA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A global LoRA gives all users the same update. MoE picks combinations from a shared pool, adding conditional capacity without storing a whole model per user. Sparse training can starve experts, so total parameter count does not establish effective capacity or ranking quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Photographers and bakers can use different expert proportions while sharing general experts. Always picking one expert reduces MoE to something close to global LoRA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d206ae586f50093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bcc8694671b1b66">Which axes and parameters must remain distinct in L2Rec&#x27;s BA updates and top-k gating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each view and expert owns A and B. Form an update shaped like the original weight, then weight it with the user gate. Select top-k on the expert axis and handle cross-view fusion separately. Shapes cannot reveal semantic/behavioral identity mismatches, and local proxy scores do not establish full expert-path training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pairing a semantic expert&#x27;s A with a behavioral expert&#x27;s B can pass shape checks but changes the mapping. Selecting users instead of experts implements another algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bcc8694671b1b66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:learn" data-paper-title="Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-learn-c99c03ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3fa0af7e5835487">Why freeze the content LLM while letting LEARN&#x27;s PCH learn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alearn">Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The LLM provides stable content semantics; recommendation objectives still need to adapt behavioral relationships. PCH reads the content sequence, models causal preference dependencies, and projects into serving space. Freezing saves cost but limits content adjustment. Pretrained semantics are not collaborative preferences and need not improve all cold-start cases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Films of the same genre may have different audiences. PCH can learn the difference from viewing order, whereas averaging frozen vectors does not train preference structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2405.03988-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3fa0af7e5835487">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:learn" data-paper-title="Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2eed10f4831732c0">Why does LEARN freeze LLM content encoding but train a causal PCH to learn preferences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alearn">Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen content encoder retains open-world semantics at lower update cost, but semantic closeness is not co-consumption. PCH learns order and next-item prediction from historical content vectors, then projects them into recommendation space. Respect history cutoffs; freezing the LLM does not mean nothing is trained or that semantic similarity proves transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two films mention adventure, but the user&#x27;s viewing sequence can reveal a more specific storytelling preference that frozen text semantics alone do not express.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2405.03988-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2eed10f4831732c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:learn" data-paper-title="Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5d6d58a64e951ab">Why isn&#x27;t LEARN&#x27;s large gain over frozen semantic mean necessarily a cold-start gain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alearn">Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mean lacks trainable preference modeling, so PCH can improve ranking by learning sequences. The source also shows strong head concentration, so gains may come from popularity rather than new-item understanding. Cold-start subgroups and matched controls are needed; overall NDCG does not prove gains for all groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recommending popular movies can substantially beat a semantic average without helping a new film reach its audience.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2405.03988-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5d6d58a64e951ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:learn" data-paper-title="Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3fecff7cba4aa75c">Is a frozen content cache enough to prevent future leakage in PCH next-item prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alearn">Knowledge Adaptation from Large Language Model to Recommendation for Practical Industrial Application</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Enforce a causal mask and cutoff in PCH: the next item belongs only on the target side and must not enter pooling. Align encoder and projection versions. Frozen parameters prevent gradient updates, not input leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Putting the test movie&#x27;s frozen vector into history before predicting it still leaks the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2405.03988-learn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3fecff7cba4aa75c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lsvcr" data-paper-title="A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-lsvcr-e1dd0222" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbc93eb9f52f98ed">Why encode video and comment consumption separately in LSVCR instead of treating comments as video metadata?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alsvcr">A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Comments have their own reading behavior and semantics. Dual sequences preserve the distinction before cross-fusion, and the training-time LLM adds personalized knowledge. Co-consumption can correlate or conflict, so better comment ranking does not prove better video ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Someone may dislike a video but enjoy its discussion. Adding comment text only to a video description can lose this independent preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13574">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.13574-lsvcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbc93eb9f52f98ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lsvcr" data-paper-title="A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-189ea1f5c254e5d0">Why give LSVCR personalized LLM preferences during training if no generative LLM runs at serving time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alsvcr">A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Video and comment semantics differ and may exceed what ID sequences capture. Cross-fusion and alignment transfer teacher knowledge into a deployable dual-sequence model. Tasks can interfere: local video and comment metrics move in different directions, so neither alone establishes overall success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A teacher can explain sarcasm in a comment during training; the serving student must judge from available sequences without secretly consulting it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13574">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.13574-lsvcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-189ea1f5c254e5d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lsvcr" data-paper-title="A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-678f95df550c57b9">What relationships do LSVCR&#x27;s SSC and VCC constrain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alsvcr">A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SSC aligns the sequential recommender&#x27;s user preferences with the LLM; VCC links video or item preferences with comment preferences. They operate across models and across objects, respectively, and can conflict. The local comment metric improved while the item metric declined; report both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learning the teacher&#x27;s photography preference is different from deciding whether a user likes photography products and photography comments equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13574">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.13574-lsvcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-678f95df550c57b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lsvcr" data-paper-title="A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccd0b0d9cfb4fb94">Why sample an ordered subset for LSVCR position encoding instead of shuffling positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alsvcr">A Large Language Model Enhanced Sequential Recommender for Joint Video and Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A short alignment sequence should cover the span of the full position table without changing chronology. An ordered subset samples uneven gaps; shuffling changes temporal relations. Cross-sequence fusion must also exclude target video and comment events not yet observed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Assign positions 3, 20, and 80 from a 1–100 table. Assigning 80, 3, and 20 instead changes which event appears newest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13574">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.13574-lsvcr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccd0b0d9cfb4fb94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-lum-66a3db6d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dc046ca11652b26">Why does LUM separate user-knowledge generation and online DLRM ranking into three stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First train a generative model on conditional user relationships; then query and cache different interests offline; finally supply knowledge vectors and target-match scores to the existing discriminative ranker. This avoids serving the large model on every request. Transfer through a DLRM interface is not necessarily lossless, and freshness and condition definitions matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Prepare multiple interest profiles offline and let the online DLRM match them to a product without replacing its real-time feature system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dc046ca11652b26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3f51ac8eb5bfaca">Why place LUM&#x27;s condition before the item being predicted rather than after the previous item as feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The condition specifies the upcoming choice&#x27;s context, query, or category and should constrain the next-item distribution. Attaching it to the previous item instead explains past behavior. LUM learns queryable user knowledge through conditional generation and extracts offline interest features for a DLRM rather than serving the full generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Entering kitchenware should condition the next cookware prediction, not be interpreted as feedback on the previous running shoe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3f51ac8eb5bfaca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-477cc9cf1c2b9611">How do LUM&#x27;s multiple conditional queries organize information differently from a fixed user embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One vector compresses all needs; conditional queries can extract distinct contexts or preferences for the downstream target. More queries require cache space and can be redundant. Gains over a sequence-free ID-DLRM include several new information sources and cannot be assigned solely to condition tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: High-rating and low-rating queries may reveal likes and dislikes separately, while an average can mix them together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-477cc9cf1c2b9611">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d46cbb9ff26d819d">Why mask query-to-query attention when appending several LUM conditions offline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each condition should independently read the same shared history. Mutual attention makes results depend on query order and breaks reuse. Predict the immediately following item from the condition output, not from an action after the item. Bind caches to the same prefix and condition version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: High- and low-rating queries should not exchange clues; reversing their order must not change the knowledge each retrieves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d46cbb9ff26d819d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lwgr" data-paper-title="LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-lwgr-831cc9dc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b637c222009ec19f">How can LWGR&#x27;s soft instruction express user differences beyond handwritten wording?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alwgr">LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / CAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Split user context into subspaces and select codewords from independent codebooks. The resulting differentiable prompt tokens and history generate user knowledge; recommendation supervision can change them. Capacity and training coverage limit personalization, and the tokens need not correspond to readable instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A photography novice and a professional may select different soft tokens even though the handwritten prompt says &#x27;analyze interests&#x27; for both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18771">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.18771-lwgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b637c222009ec19f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lwgr" data-paper-title="LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e153cabf62c29685">Why does LWGR learn personalized soft instructions while limiting degradation against a frozen reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alwgr">LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / CAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed prompt cannot adapt across users. Subspace codebooks produce trainable soft tokens to personalize knowledge extraction. LLM knowledge can conflict with behavioral evidence, so the frozen reference anchors a confidence degradation constraint; nearline computation controls serving cost. Learned prompts do not make extracted knowledge true or more reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two travelers care about price and photography respectively. Soft prompts can retrieve different knowledge, while the constraint should discourage new evidence from overriding reliable existing scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18771">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.18771-lwgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e153cabf62c29685">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lwgr" data-paper-title="LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7040336605d65fd">What does LWGR&#x27;s reference confidence constraint protect compared with ordinary KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alwgr">LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / CAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It penalizes the amount by which a positive target&#x27;s mean token log-probability falls below the reference tolerance. KL instead measures whole-distribution drift. Updating the multiplier is not sufficient: locally λ changed without an improvement in degradation, so protection was not demonstrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Moving probability to another reasonable candidate may raise KL without much target damage; a large target drop directly activates the one-sided constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18771">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.18771-lwgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7040336605d65fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lwgr" data-paper-title="LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c6d7ced9871671c">How should LWGR&#x27;s straight-through code selection and dual update be checked separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alwgr">LWGR: Lagrangian-Constrained Personalized World Knowledge for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / CAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use hard codes forward and soft-distribution gradients backward; verify soft-instruction parameters change. Update λ using C−ε and project to nonnegative values. A rising multiplier signals violation, not satisfaction. Frozen reference, BOS fusion, and nearline cache are separate interfaces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If C remains above tolerance while λ rises, report failure to satisfy the constraint. A hard index cutting gradients also prevents learning even though it selects codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18771">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.18771-lwgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c6d7ced9871671c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<span id="paper-recommendation-m6rec-d70d1b1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-948a8e376d11e409">Why turn anonymous behavior and candidates into natural language for M6-Rec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A text interface lets one pretrained model receive different recommendation problems. Options and adapters encode task differences without maintaining a full model per scenario. Retrieval, explanation, and classification still have distinct outputs and decoding costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same model can make a yes/no movie recommendation and explain it; explanation accuracy is not retrieval hit rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d3a6b15d0fd72c8">What do option tuning and adapters change in M6-Rec&#x27;s multitask setup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The frozen backbone preserves pretrained capability. Option parameters provide a small task decision interface, and layerwise adapters add compact task-specific transforms. Shared parameter-efficient adaptation does not automatically make inference cheap; edge deployment needs separate compression and serving design. Local small tasks do not demonstrate full giant-M6 transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Use different options and adapters for relevance and content explanation on one frozen model, but both still execute the large backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d3a6b15d0fd72c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2a1ebcf2997bc76">What does option-adapter tuning learn beyond option tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Option prototypes mainly change the output decision interface. Adapters add low-rank nonlinear transformations between frozen layers and can adapt intermediate representations. They still use far fewer parameters than full fine-tuning, but the small and variable local trend does not establish stable production gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Moving yes/no prototypes changes the ruler; adapters can change the features it measures. The two arms do not have identical parameter budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2a1ebcf2997bc76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e1fdaea7f5556ee">Why check normalization and temperature for M6-Rec&#x27;s local frozen-backbone binary option scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The source scores normalized representations against trainable prototypes, with temperature controlling the class distribution. Without normalization, norms can change the mechanism. Freeze both backbones and update only options and permitted adapters. BERT-tiny is a reduced task path, not full generative M6.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unrestricted prototype can win by growing its norm instead of learning direction; normalization and temperature enforce the defined scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:marc" data-paper-title="Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
