<span id="paper-recommendation-marc-216b86ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-23b84a11d274b3f0">Why might MARC choose an intermediate layer instead of assuming the LLM&#x27;s final layer is best?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amarc">Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final layers specialize in pretraining outputs. MRA observations motivate separating compression and adaptation to remove proxy-task interference while retaining recommendation information. Select layers on validation; middle layers are not universally superior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A middle layer may distinguish two user groups better in a compact representation even if the final layer is best at predicting words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18146">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.18146-marc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23b84a11d274b3f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:marc" data-paper-title="Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7980095d4e002eb">Why separate representation compression from recommendation adaptation in MARC, and why might an intermediate LLM layer be chosen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amarc">Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The last layer favors the language objective, whereas an intermediate layer can retain more compressible general features. What compression preserves is not necessarily what recommendation needs. Separate modules and information constraints distinguish dimensional cost from task relevance. Intermediate-layer superiority must be measured per model and dataset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The final layer excels at next-word prediction, but a middle layer may retain product use. Reconstruction alone can preserve costly language details irrelevant to purchase preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18146">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.18146-marc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7980095d4e002eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:marc" data-paper-title="Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c62caff06e1cb6d1">What are the benefits and risks of separate MARC compression and adaptation versus one linear reducer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amarc">Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One projection conflates information loss with task learning. Separate modules make each effect measurable, but add choices and objective interactions. Removing a supposed nuisance can delete useful signals. The public proxy was negative, so information constraints alone do not establish generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Removing content-specific style may help matching unless style itself drives user preference. Ablate both stages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18146">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.18146-marc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c62caff06e1cb6d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:marc" data-paper-title="Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-db89084985cb4dc0">How should MARC avoid mixing validation and test during layer and nuisance-projection selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amarc">Modular Representation Compression: Adapting LLMs for Efficient and Effective Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate directions from training data and choose layer, dimension, and removed directions on validation, then freeze for test. Match projections to the selected hidden-state space. A fixed-score proxy without full information-objective training must be described within that boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Choosing the highest test NDCG layer turns test into tuning. Pick it first, then check transfer on independent data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18146">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.18146-marc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db89084985cb4dc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mim-fdc0fc79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-167d9287d182fc2d">Why align content with interest after multimodal reconstruction in MIM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction teaches recoverable features, not their relation to user preference. Content-interest-aware SFT links semantic and collaborative information; CiUBM combines content and ID interests. Low reconstruction loss cannot substitute for ranking evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recovering poster colors does not identify a preference for hard science fiction over comedy without behavioral supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-167d9287d182fc2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8fa8489000b3a6e">Why follow multimodal masked reconstruction with content-interest-aware SFT in MIM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction learns internal content structure but not which differences users care about. SFT aligns semantic features with consumption interests, then content and ID interest fuse to combine cold-start and collaborative signals. Reconstruction alone does not establish ranking relevance, and either branch can overwhelm the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reconstructing product color does not show whether users care about lightness or durability. Interest alignment introduces consumption evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8fa8489000b3a6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccaad5564c0af13b">What cold-start clues does MIM&#x27;s dual-interest fusion add beyond ID co-occurrence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ID co-occurrence needs feedback; shared multimodal semantics can transfer to sparse items. Content noise and bad mappings can hurt ranking. Local NDCG rose slightly while Hit fell, so report both and evaluate a dedicated new-item cohort.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unseen movie may be identified as science fiction from content, but a misleading action poster can also hurt otherwise sound ID scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccaad5564c0af13b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3115f2398f8704fd">Why use different visibility rules for MIM masked reconstruction and recommendation targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can mask content and reconstruct it, but recommendation input stops at the current history cutoff. Future items and feedback are targets only. Modality masking cannot fix a future item already present in the user representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Masking part of a historical poster is valid content training; putting the test film&#x27;s full vector in history before predicting it leaks the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3115f2398f8704fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mm-llm-7bcb82aa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-933964f78c96769a">Why normalize MM-LLM captions into categorical token IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free-form descriptions vary in wording and length. Category IDs provide a stable cacheable interface for ID, visual, and history-profile fusion. Normalization loses detail and inherits caption errors, so discrete IDs are not ground-truth annotations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Camping in rain&#x27; and &#x27;putting up a tent in the rain&#x27; can map to similar tokens; a false weather caption produces a false tag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-933964f78c96769a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ea845fc58225065">Why turn visual content into normalized semantic tokens in MM-LLM instead of running a large model per ranking request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visual vectors are rich but fine-grained semantics can be hard to use consistently. The offline visual encoder, Q-Former, and LM generate captions normalized into reusable category tokens. A smaller online ranker combines them with IDs and visual features, amortizing semantic compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Extract rain, camping, and gear tutorial tokens offline from a thumbnail, then rank using those features and history without asking the LM to explain the image again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ea845fc58225065">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16be0a596f577f16">What can MM-LLM caption tokens add beyond visual embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous visual representations retain perceptual structure; captions extract language-level attributes and uses. They can duplicate or contradict each other, motivating gated rather than blind fusion. The local caption ablation was near flat and Hit fell, so readability is not evidence of ranking gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The visual vector reflects color and layout; a caption can identify a waterproofing demo or add noise if it contributes no new concept.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16be0a596f577f16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-236a3f04620a3cd6">Why are MM-LLM&#x27;s four local caption tokens not a full visual–LLaMA2 training reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public content vectors replace private images, and light query cross-attention generates proxy tokens. This tests reduced fusion without the original visual encoder, Q-Former, or full large model. Report internal ID+content and DIN comparisons separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four tokens made from genres do not demonstrate image understanding, even if fusion loss falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-236a3f04620a3cd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mosaic-eb607f0f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8998ade858b0c37d">Why isn&#x27;t Mosaic&#x27;s specialist fleet equivalent to widening one general user embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memory, dense interaction, sequence, and downstream co-training specialists optimize different knowledge and can evolve independently. Downstream consumers select interfaces. One wider model can still be dominated by one objective. A fleet adds storage and maintenance and does not guarantee independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A memory specialist recalls brands, a sequence specialist detects this week&#x27;s trip, and a jointly trained specialist adapts to purchases; width alone need not separate these roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8998ade858b0c37d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc7d4916c8920301">Why penalize redundancy in a new Mosaic specialist when several user embeddings already exist?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New networks can repeat old knowledge while adding serving cost. Mosaic forms a representation fleet, mines task relations to learn joint behavior, and penalizes duplication against existing vectors. The goal is complementary information for downstream readers; geometric orthogonality does not imply business independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If old vectors already remember brands, a new specialist could learn when users explore instead of remembering the same brands again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc7d4916c8920301">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c49d70463f59f969">What supervision does Mosaic&#x27;s MRM joint label add beyond independent binary tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Marginal labels constrain individual frequencies, whereas Cartesian-product labels represent which events co-occur. Related-task mining selects useful combinations, and label space can grow. Joint association does not establish causality; exposure can influence both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks and long views can each happen half the time together or disjointly. Marginals alone cannot distinguish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c49d70463f59f969">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1753a2d5f97516bd">Why warm up Mosaic&#x27;s cosine redundancy loss and evaluate complementarity separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong early separation can make untrained features diverge randomly. Warm-up lets task information form before reducing overlap. Lower or negative cosine shows geometry, not useful new evidence. Preserve the local Hit decrease and head-share increase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Random vectors can be uncorrelated and useless for ranking. First learn meaningful interests, then verify that another specialist adds value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1753a2d5f97516bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-msd-3339b303" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fb8ddb268dd09af">Why split MSD&#x27;s MKDM and MKIM into knowledge distillation and CTR adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher keyword and reasoning generation transfers semantics first. LoRA and the recommendation adapter then align those features to clicks, unlike frozen knowledge. Supervision and trainable parameters differ across stages; lower distillation loss does not guarantee higher CTR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: First learn what warmth and commuting mean for coats, then train how user clicks combine them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fb8ddb268dd09af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-517fad13ebc6e70b">Why distill teacher keywords and reasoning and then align the student to CTR in MSD rather than cache teacher embeddings alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Static embeddings save compute but do not adapt to CTR. Autoregressive distillation transfers teacher semantics; LoRA and a recommendation adapter learn task features. Cache frequent items, encode misses online, and fuse only relevant history. These address semantics, CTR, and serving separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A student learns coat warmth and commuting attributes from teacher text, adapts them using clicks, then serves cached popular coats and encodes new items online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-517fad13ebc6e70b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e66fc937b374d9f9">How does MSD amortize compute with frequent-item caching and online encoding for rare items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent items yield cache reuse; online encoding preserves coverage for rare items and misses. Encoding everything online is fresher but repeats expensive work. Stale cache/LoRA versions, refreshes, and hit rate matter. The local path does not measure production embedding efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cache a coat scored a million times a day, encode a new raincoat online, and refresh cached semantics when LoRA changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e66fc937b374d9f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de515730baa43a9">Why separately check candidate-specific top-three history and shareable cache features in MSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History selection depends on target similarity and can differ per candidate; cached item semantics must not include user or candidate-pair interaction. Verify only designated LoRA parameters update in the frozen student. Mixing paths can contaminate caches or erase candidate relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cameras need photography history and shoes need running history. Their selected top-three sets cannot be shared even if base item encodings can.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de515730baa43a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-muchator-f63c99f7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d872f4ff94de9805">Why treat MuChaToR as conversational music recommendation instead of just next-track prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current mood, context, and willingness to explore may differ from history. Dialogue can clarify needs, domain pretraining adds music knowledge, and SFT/RL connect interactions. Fluent discussion is not evidence of taste fit; evaluate separately and ground to a valid catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Something relaxing for my commute, but not only old songs&#x27; requires both mood matching and exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d872f4ff94de9805">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c20977be1c72097">Why does MuChaToR optimize intent, discovery, and dialogue rewards beyond music pretraining and instruction learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Music pretraining adds domain knowledge and instructions teach response format, but neither resolves immediate preference versus discovery. RL provides feedback for intent, discovery, and dialogue with a reference constraint. The local ranking proxy does not demonstrate actual music conversation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For relaxed commute music without only old songs, reward both mood fit and some discovery rather than merely imitating familiar artists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c20977be1c72097">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ab48c3662179e27">How can MuChaToR discovery reward conflict with intent matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strict matching may repeat familiar content, while too much discovery promotes irrelevant novelty. Dialogue quality can favor polished explanations too. Multi-objective optimization and KL balance trade-offs; one reward gain does not establish satisfaction. A movie proxy lacks music dialogue feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Experimental music may be novel but poor for a quiet commute; familiar pop may fit without discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ab48c3662179e27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bdf37c113e2ddfe">Why can&#x27;t local MovieLens results validate MuChaToR music pretraining and dialogue RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The proxy lacks actual music corpora, dialogue turns, and reward environments. Fixed-candidate NDCG measures only the scoring path that ran. Dialogue training requires actual updates and valid logs. Keep negative proxy results instead of replacing them with paper business outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Genre features can test an interface without proving the model understands harmony or can clarify playlist needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bdf37c113e2ddfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-music-rationales-61aa6d5c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fcfcf53f4a25dd8">Why include unplayed artists and personalized reasons in a Music Rationales discovery profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A reason connects unfamiliar candidates with known interests. Generate nomination and explanation asynchronously, then verify entities and trustworthiness. It supports discovery, not guaranteed taste fit, and must not invent history to persuade.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Explain how an artist relates to piano trios the user plays, but do not claim a prior listen absent from history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fcfcf53f4a25dd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2c4588e9452cf62">Why generate Music Rationales offline and separately test nomination and showing rationales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline generation uses full history and expensive reasoning, then normalizes entities and filters rationales for cached serving. Nomination changes candidates; showing reasons can change response to the same candidates. Separate arms identify which path contributed. Fluency does not establish trustworthy reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Show the same unfamiliar jazz artist with or without a reference to the user&#x27;s piano-trio taste to isolate the reason&#x27;s effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2c4588e9452cf62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a76079ab40e8461">What questions do explanation-only with fixed CF ordering and LLM-first nomination answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nomination changes coverage and position and can affect offline hits. Adding explanations to the same list keeps offline Hit identical; only rationale coverage can be checked offline. Actual behavioral response needs a user experiment. Separate arms prevent misattribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding reasons for the same five artists cannot change static Hit@5 but might change click behavior under real exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a76079ab40e8461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f97298e1fc83f412">Why retain rejection and cache-miss states in Music Rationales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize artists to a real catalog, reject unsupported explanations, and fall back to the original recommender on a cache miss rather than inventing text. Evaluate nominations separately from final fallback lists. A single-seed diagnostic without explanation CTR cannot establish user benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fall back to CF on a nonexistent artist rather than force a mistaken name match; fallback availability is not LLM nomination success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f97298e1fc83f412">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:netflix-mediafm" data-paper-title="Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-netflix-mediafm-31c991d9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e014134d24b2b7e0">Why does MediaFM provide shared media features rather than final recommendation probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anetflix-mediafm">Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multimodal features describe content, while downstream towers adapt them to users, queries, and task objectives. Freezing avoids duplicate computation but limits missing details. Verify feature reuse separately from business outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same poster vector supports home artwork and search, but high similarity does not make it optimal in every context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18322">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18322-netflix-mediafm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e014134d24b2b7e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:netflix-mediafm" data-paper-title="Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a14f7828b81c132">Why freeze shared multimodal features across Netflix MediaFM tasks rather than train a separate visual model for each?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anetflix-mediafm">Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A reusable feature layer amortizes media understanding. Downstream towers adapt users, queries, and assets, with query similarity complementing personalization in search. Sharing reduces duplicate encoding but cannot recover visual details absent from frozen features. Offline screening does not replace online validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reuse a poster vector for home artwork and search; emphasize query match for &#x27;seaside comedy&#x27; and long-term taste on home.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18322">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18322-netflix-mediafm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a14f7828b81c132">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:netflix-mediafm" data-paper-title="Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-065b8f3cc5f30c5a">How does query similarity add current search intent beyond user-only personalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anetflix-mediafm">Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User similarity reflects long-term taste; query similarity adds the explicit current request. Balance them so neither erases the other. This does not establish a universal weight, and offline IPS and winner proxies do not replace online evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user who likes action searches for a warm comedy. Query match should override some action preference to keep search artwork relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18322">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18322-netflix-mediafm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-065b8f3cc5f30c5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:netflix-mediafm" data-paper-title="Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b81e344e6b05c3a">Why calibrate all three vector scales when MediaFM combines two dot products?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anetflix-mediafm">Multimedia Asset Personalization via Multimodal Embeddings at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User, query, and asset vectors need comparable scales or explicit calibration, otherwise one norm dominates the nominal α. Select checkpoints and fusion weights without tuning on test and bind frozen features to versions. Local movie-content proxies are not the production multimodal pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A query norm ten times larger can dominate a nominal 50/50 mix; normalization makes the coefficients interpretable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18322">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18322-netflix-mediafm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b81e344e6b05c3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:notellm" data-paper-title="NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-notellm-9364e133" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2cf64a8c96cdbab5">Why is NoteLLM&#x27;s compression token both a retrieval and generation interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anotellm">NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrastive retrieval and label generation use the same compressed state, requiring collaborative and semantic evidence. If generation bypasses it to read raw text, the constraint changes. Compression does not preserve every note detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A token must bring co-read notes together and still generate &#x27;camping gear,&#x27; not just encode shared popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2cf64a8c96cdbab5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:notellm" data-paper-title="NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb498d5617532d9c">Why train NoteLLM&#x27;s compression state on co-read contrastive learning and content generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anotellm">NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Co-read pairs capture collaborative relations but contrastive similarity alone can lose fine semantics. Generating tags and categories from the same bottleneck forces it to preserve recoverable content. The two objectives shape a retrieval vector that does not merely memorize co-occurrence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Tent and cookware notes can be close for campers yet retain enough detail to generate distinct tags.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb498d5617532d9c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:notellm" data-paper-title="NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fe13bdf9a3534e6">What relation does GCL co-reading add beyond text-similarity positives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anotellm">NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text similarity is content-driven; co-reading links consumption across superficially different notes but can reflect exposure and popularity. CSFT constrains content retention. Complementarity is not absence of bias, and simplified labels do not reproduce real hashtag generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Tent reviews and camp recipes may be co-read despite different text, whereas two near-identical tent reviews are textual matches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fe13bdf9a3534e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:notellm" data-paper-title="NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-818da7eef23dbbae">How verify NoteLLM&#x27;s contrastive vector and CSFT initial state use the same compression position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anotellm">NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Read the same special-token hidden state for both, not a last position for one and mean for the other. Align batch pairs and causal generation masks and exclude padding. Frozen versus joint training tests representations, not a full DIN ranking comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Title-mean contrastive features and an independent CLS for generation can both train without constraining the same bottleneck.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-open-web-ufm-467147f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f33b067fd0273ebc">Why can&#x27;t Open Web UFM assume a stable long-term user ID and complete history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RTB identity depends on permissions, platforms, and privacy, creating short disconnected paths. Learn transferable features from limited browsing for CTR and auction tasks. Logged-in MovieLens histories cannot directly verify open-web identity modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One person can appear as several short device-specific paths. Do not silently reconstruct a universal ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f33b067fd0273ebc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad5326f868c277b5">Why jointly train masked prediction and sequence contrastive learning in Open Web UFM rather than one CTR label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masking recovers local events from partial context; contrastive views teach whole-sequence consistency. Pretraining can support CTR and win-rate heads with sparse labels. Identity discontinuity and privacy affect input distribution; a local zero gain is not evidence of cross-task benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A three-visit trajectory without click labels still supports masked recovery and two-view positives before fitting a small CTR head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad5326f868c277b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa71a813cea60613">What kinds of consistency do masked recovery and sequence InfoNCE enforce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MLM predicts missing events from local context, while contrastive learning aligns whole-trajectory views. They complement each other but strong corruptions or false negatives can mislead. The local zero result does not verify transfer merely because both losses exist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Nearby visits can recover one masked visit, and partial trajectories can retain the same intent, unless the views now represent genuinely different needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa71a813cea60613">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3a95c8f2ee5f83e">Why make UFM recipe lifters auditable rather than let them change data and evaluation freely?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Define permitted changes to attribute feedback while preserving budgets and data contracts. Changing examples or metrics can create fake gains; LLM proposals cannot edit answers. Retain the zero result under the same encoder and 45 steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Varying mask rate is comparable; deleting hard test users changes the task rather than improving pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3a95c8f2ee5f83e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pin-scale-f40ee8a5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e632fcb5a486d1d0">Why use hierarchical SIDs for discriminative dense retrieval in Pin-SCALE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cascading pooling maps transferable coarse and fine semantic codes into a retrieval embedding, and engagement/multi-view losses align it to the task. Discriminative nearest neighbors do not require autoregressive code decoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pool gardening and indoor-plant codes into a two-tower vector instead of generating two codes at serving time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
