<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e632fcb5a486d1d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-44d732d6513a5be6">Why retain residual Semantic ID levels and add engagement and multi-view supervision in Pin-SCALE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content codes transfer to new items but are not necessarily discriminative for behavior. Residual hierarchy and cascading pooling preserve coarse-to-fine details, while engagement, query–item, and item–item objectives align codes to recommendation. SIDs participate in training, not just replace vectors with integers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two living-room posts share a coarse theme but need finer audience distinctions; engagement and co-occurrence can refine them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44d732d6513a5be6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f1b52aab5ba2f5b">How does engagement-aware tokenization differ from pure content reconstruction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction preserves content geometry; engagement emphasizes differences affecting consumption. It can introduce exposure and popularity bias, so check tail generalization. The local fresh cohort&#x27;s small denominator prevents interpreting large relative changes as industrial gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Behavior can distinguish similar renovation images by user purpose but may also favor a popular style over new content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f1b52aab5ba2f5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c46a225e046b55e5">Why doesn&#x27;t one sample&#x27;s positive layer weight wi necessarily change Pin-SCALE nearest-code argmin?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiplying all distances by the same positive scalar leaves their order unchanged. The weight may instead change codebook updates or global learning. Check where it is applied; zero and candidate-dependent weights are different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Multiplying distances two and five by three still selects two. Later assignment can change if weighted learning moves centers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c46a225e046b55e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinclip-b1beb580" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f7bc96645434ce7">Why connect new PinCLIP content to the recommendation graph through content vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New items lack collaboration. Existing board neighbors teach platform semantics and the content encoder transfers them to unseen items. Fine image–text detail helps, but graph exposure bias remains. Evaluate cold start separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unclicked lamp can connect to décor-board furniture through content; that is not an observed co-purchase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f7bc96645434ce7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-909083d23461a8ae">Why add Pin–Board neighbor alignment beyond image–text alignment in PinCLIP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic image–text alignment captures content compatibility, while user boards expose platform-specific relationships. Neighbor supervision adds graph semantics and multigranular features retain details for new content. Exposure bias can persist, so graph alignment is not unbiased preference estimation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A table and a lamp may look different but share Scandinavian décor boards, letting a new lamp connect to related furniture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-909083d23461a8ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1408018090c68888">Where do PinCLIP positives come from in neighbor alignment versus image–text contrastive learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Image–text positives link modalities of one item; graph neighbors link distinct items on boards, learning pairing and interest structure. Signals can conflict, requiring weights and sampling. A sparse genre proxy cannot reproduce VLM distinctions, so its negative result is bounded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A lamp&#x27;s image and description are one positive pair; the lamp and a table on one board are another, not the same item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1408018090c68888">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a3b464cdc396da7">Why exclude future test edges from PinCLIP graph training rather than just freeze the image encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future consumption edges can encode target relations even without encoder updates. Graph construction, negatives, and new-content splits need cutoffs. Distinguish local alignment from original pretraining; vector shape alone does not establish fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding a future saved lamp edge exposes the answer before prediction regardless of frozen parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a3b464cdc396da7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinterest-ads-llm-d99be125" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7200a906a9dc8325">Are Pinterest Ads LLM advertisers and interests one-to-one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Advertisers are entities and interests are themes; one advertiser spans many topics and one topic many advertisers. Outputs provide different features and retrieval clues. Neither represents an observed conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camping can involve several brands and a department store can sell camping and home items; the topic is not one brand ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27856">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27856-pinterest-ads-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7200a906a9dc8325">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b124905c1042fcc">Why predict auxiliary advertisers and interests in Pinterest Ads LLM rather than replace real-time ad ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline user profiles and cross-source history predict conversion-oriented advertisers and interests for supplementary retrieval and conversion features. SFT predicts the next advertiser; GRPO uses hit position and length rewards. Daily batch inference stays outside requests, while real-time scoring and auction remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An overnight camping-brand prediction adds a channel and feature; online conversion scoring and auctions still choose the ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27856">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27856-pinterest-ads-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b124905c1042fcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-654736ff6cb03e48">Why separate SFT+GRPO versus SFT from LLM features versus two-tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One compares advertiser generation post-training; the other measures downstream integration. Baselines and metrics differ. GRPO did not improve Recall, feature AUC improved slightly, and the supplemental quota was zero. This is not success at every stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A generator can stay flat while its log-probability helps prediction. That does not justify more retrieval candidates or imply Recall improved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27856">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27856-pinterest-ads-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-654736ff6cb03e48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f2c2561b0e640a5">Why check output-length and hit-position rewards together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position rewards put correct advertisers early; length penalties prevent longer lists from gaming hits. Deduplicate parsed outputs and count advertisers and interests separately, with the reduced five-item rule explicit. Preserve validation&#x27;s SFT or zero-quota choices instead of retuning on test mean rank.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fifty brands may include the target but violate a five-brand budget; a hit alone would reward that loophole.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27856">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.27856-pinterest-ads-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f2c2561b0e640a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pit-181d335d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8772b022688e6020">Why can distribution drift make old PIT SID paths inappropriate even when item text is unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Needs, inventory, and interaction frequency change, weakening the old mapping to the generative distribution. Distinguish actual data drift, model updates, and address changes from random variation. One fluctuation does not prove recoding is needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same light coat serves spring commuting and autumn travel; a fixed random seed cannot remove changing preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8772b022688e6020">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecc9ec54ecfeaba4">Why retain multiple SIDs per item and choose by recommendation loss in PIT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fixed code constrains all users to one semantic path and may drift out of fit. PIT jointly trains tokenizer and recommender and selects among codes by recommendation loss. A one-to-many index preserves choices but complicates mapping and deduplication; multiple paths are not multiple items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Office stretches may be reachable via fitness or desk health. Route by user, then merge both paths to the same video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecc9ec54ecfeaba4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c388d254bbd06a28">Where do gradients couple PIT&#x27;s tokenizer and recommender compared with a frozen codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen generator adapts to existing codes; PIT uses recommendation loss in code selection and learning, adapting paths to preference. This can destabilize addresses, so track versions and drift. Neither lossless streaming updates nor universal inferiority from a local negative proxy is established.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep an office-use entry for a fitness video if recommendation supervision supports it; a frozen index can only change probabilities on existing paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c388d254bbd06a28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52b4d03ec7d37f66">Why use PIT&#x27;s user-guided minimum-loss choice only among training candidate codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Argmin can use training labels to select a supervisory path, but inference must use model probabilities and legal beam paths rather than gold loss. Alternate codes map back to the same item. Gold-guided code choice is answer-aware routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Knowing the correct video and picking its easiest code inflates Hit. Generate codes before checking the item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52b4d03ec7d37f66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-precise-dd30948e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ddcf43cd4f766e7">Why do PRECISE UT and TT address all-scenario interests and sparse targets separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broad sequence training supplies base preferences and target training adapts scarce labels. Objectives and attention rules differ, and transfer can hurt cold/tail items. Overall local gains accompanied lower Cold Recall, not universal cold-start improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn interests from all positive feedback and then tune on high ratings. Popularity may improve aggregate hits while missing new films.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ddcf43cd4f766e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74ac61e57c3c2e60">Why train IDs with frozen text representations before joint unfreezing in PRECISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong pretrained text can dominate initially random IDs and leave collaborative structure unlearned. The frozen stage lets IDs learn distinctions before joint adaptation. All-scene pretraining and sparse-target tuning address transfer separately; overall gains do not guarantee cold or tail gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two similar movie descriptions can attract different audiences; learning IDs first can capture that difference before fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74ac61e57c3c2e60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-01d083c1aec8b3be">What details does PRECISE token-attention MoE retain compared with averaging text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token experts can focus on distinct spans and top-k routing can combine perspectives, while averaging flattens them. Experts can duplicate one another and strong text can suppress IDs, motivating the frozen-text stage. Validate complementarity and cold/tail outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Different experts can preserve &#x27;beginner&#x27; versus &#x27;professional&#x27;; experts all reading celebrity names do not retain meaningful detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01d083c1aec8b3be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fbde951e57959a36">Why must PRECISE still exclude target items when switching from causal UT to noncausal TT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TT can read observed history bidirectionally, not the held-out target. Remove the target before constructing the sequence; the concatenation MLP sees legal positions only. Repeated in-batch items must not be treated as mutually exclusive negatives, as fixed in source.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Historical A and B can attend to one another, while test C remains outside the input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fbde951e57959a36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:proximity-features" data-paper-title="Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-proximity-features-c055e9e4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-41229477669023db">Why are Proximity Features group keys rather than anonymous personal IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aproximity-features">Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keys aggregate geographic groups meeting count thresholds, with denser regions split and sparser ones merged. Serving consumes group behavior without persistent individual tracking. Cohort priors miss fine individual preferences, and proxy ZIP counts are not production privacy thresholds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Nearby users&#x27; short-stay preferences can seed an anonymous request without identifying one user&#x27;s bookings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12246-proximity-features/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41229477669023db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:proximity-features" data-paper-title="Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b212bc7d176d0cc">Why split dense regions and merge sparse regions in Airbnb proximity keys?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aproximity-features">Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed grid can be too coarse downtown and contain too few users elsewhere. Hash subdivision and coarser merging maintain group support. Daily aggregates provide anonymous cold-start priors, not persistent personal identity. Geography proxies cohort preferences, not individual interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Split a block with thousands of users, but enlarge an equally sized suburban cell with ten people.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12246-proximity-features/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b212bc7d176d0cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:proximity-features" data-paper-title="Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d24a218d06f62fb0">What does Airbnb proximity aggregation add beyond a global cold-start aggregate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aproximity-features">Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global aggregates give all anonymous requests one prior. Proximity aggregates condition on nearby groups with adequate support. They capture local demand but reduce samples per bucket and may amplify regional bias. ZIP proxies test local signals, not recovered personal tastes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A group may favor weekend trips while the global population favors large cities; one traveler in that group can still want an international trip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12246-proximity-features/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d24a218d06f62fb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:proximity-features" data-paper-title="Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-61996e1d79f98663">Why version proximity coordinate quantization, hashes, and daily aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aproximity-features">Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Group behavior is accumulated by stable keys. Changing precision or hashing can move a region to a new bucket and mismatch serving history. Handle small groups and missing coordinates explicitly, without secretly using precise personal locations. Small MovieLens buckets are not production groups of around a thousand or privacy evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Changing decimal precision today and looking up yesterday&#x27;s key can read the wrong aggregate; successful base64 encoding proves little.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12246">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12246-proximity-features/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-61996e1d79f98663">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-quasid-4adc5716" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b938437696f2b972">Does a larger QuaSID distance imply one item is preferred?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Margin and eligibility indicate which pairs need distinguishable addresses, not user preference direction. Both items can be relevant or irrelevant. User-conditioned scoring still determines ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two delivery eligibility classes can separate cleanly without making either item desirable to the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b938437696f2b972">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-021d39c8f232816f">Why use business-eligibility-dependent collision margins in QuaSID instead of repelling every similar item equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nearby codes share semantics, but collisions can confuse items that must remain distinct in serving. Eligibility weights allocate separation where it matters, including sparse items, while uniform repulsion wastes capacity and breaks useful neighborhoods. Outcomes still depend on signal quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Nearly identical items may share a coarse code but need different fine codes for distinct delivery eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-021d39c8f232816f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a10a25b1f687f6f">How do differentiated QuaSID margins allocate code space compared with uniform collision repulsion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform pressure can waste capacity and damage semantic neighborhoods. Eligibility-weighted separations prioritize business requirements, but depend on accurate and current eligibility. The public proxy regressed slightly; design specificity is not measured improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Separate items with incompatible inventory eligibility, but erroneous eligibility could split otherwise useful substitutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a10a25b1f687f6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a6a211e585fea57">Why stop pushing QuaSID distances after the margin?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>[mij−d]+ is zero beyond the margin: enough separation is the goal. Align qij and margin with the same pair and use training-visible eligibility. Fix distance and symmetry conventions; do not derive favorable pairs from test eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Always minimizing negative distance would repel already-separated codes and destroy useful semantic structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a6a211e585fea57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recap-84f36c5b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e280fb604e68e0c">Are RECAP&#x27;s LLM judge and two-tower evaluator the same role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The judge screens behavior pairs for label consistency to create training data. The two-tower evaluator learns profile–behavior matching and provides update rewards. Either can be wrong and neither is true user satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge can approve a pair, but saying &#x27;good&#x27; does not train a deployable two-tower reward model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e280fb604e68e0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b85fc63690d9f881">Why separate RECAP LLM semantic edits and deterministic lifecycle management, then train from recommendation feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The LLM interprets new behavior but cannot guarantee capacity, merging, or eviction. A state machine enforces lifecycle while the LLM edits semantics. An evaluator rewards usefulness for future behavior instead of summary resemblance. Proxy bias can still be amplified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Update running to cycling after new behavior and let rules evict stale entries; reward better prediction of later cycling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b85fc63690d9f881">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e8ae9dc0e877508">Why can closed-loop RECAP GRPO increase reward while test ranking falls relative to open-loop SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT imitates updates, whereas GRPO optimizes evaluator preferences. If the proxy diverges from true next-item behavior, optimizing it can hurt generalization. This happened locally. Use independent evaluation plus reference, format, and diversity constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge that likes detailed interests can reward verbosity while the user&#x27;s main need gets diluted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e8ae9dc0e877508">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a0b55f001b5c722">Who should enforce RECAP capacity |Pt|≤C, and why isn&#x27;t a prompt sufficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deterministic state machine enforces lifecycle, merges, and evictions after validating LLM output. Bind updates, evidence, and rewards to the same round and exclude future targets. Expose invalid format and overflow rather than silently masking failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If seven entries arrive for capacity four, reject or merge by rule and log it; silent truncation does not prove compliance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a0b55f001b5c722">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-mobile-6c2409d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3538151a4afc483">Why run behavior-to-query on-device but keep RecGPT-Mobile retrieval server-side?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local context can generate a query with a small quantized model without sending raw history. The server maintains the large catalog. Devices still pay energy, compute, and updates. Privacy depends on actual transmission, not the label on-device.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Send a camping-light query, not the browsing log that generated it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3538151a4afc483">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d40e87b3bf547f6">Why regenerate RecGPT-Mobile queries only when joint drift passes a threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On-device inference still costs battery and time. Entropy, overlap, and divergence test meaningful intent changes, and a prompt budget limits per-call cost. The device converts behavior to intent and the server retrieves; gating may miss subtle important shifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Repeated shoe views need not trigger repeatedly, while switching to baby products can trigger a new server query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d40e87b3bf547f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-020a897cd156903d">Why are INT8 storage reduction and INT8 inference speed distinct evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eight-bit serialization reduces file size; dequantizing to float kernels can leave runtime unchanged or slower. True quantized compute needs supported hardware and operators. The Mac did not enable INT8 linear, so half storage is not half latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A compressed file saves transfer while unpacking and generation still take time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-020a897cd156903d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d7a9b183c9fd8b1">How verify RecGPT-Mobile&#x27;s prompt budget and drift trigger separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select components by marginal gain within a token cap, and trigger by entropy, Jaccard, and JS changes. These govern per-call cost and call frequency. Future test queries cannot choose either. Small-sample semantic accuracy is not device interaction success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A needed refresh does not permit an unlimited prompt; even a short prompt need not be recomputed if intent is stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d7a9b183c9fd8b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-v2-f68ee63c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-649ef68870c76939">Which RecGPT-V2 inputs are evidence and which are reasoning instructions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compressed behavior summarizes observations; the meta-prompt specifies how to use them. Instructions can shift attention but cannot create facts or recover lost evidence reliably. Preserve this boundary across agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Use &#x27;prioritize discovery&#x27; or &#x27;prioritize practical choices&#x27; on the same history without inventing a diving trip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1de662783c54e13">Why use hierarchical agents and dynamic meta-prompts rather than several fixed reasoning chains in RecGPT-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed chains can repeat interests and ignore context. Hierarchical agents separate intents, compress behavior, and construct task-specific prompts so paths specialize. Rewards and judges help refine outputs, but agent count does not ensure independent knowledge; check repetition, bias, and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Extract travel and photography needs separately instead of repeating &#x27;likes photography&#x27; across three templates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1de662783c54e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5830fcd0732f5656">How do agent judges and real user feedback differ in evaluation bias?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Judges quickly score semantics or format; users reveal behavior, but exposure biases it. Mixed rewards can use both without treating either as true satisfaction. Self-proposal and self-judging can reinforce bias, requiring independent validation. Local proxies do not establish production judging/RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge may like long explanations while users want quick results. Record semantic scores separately from behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5830fcd0732f5656">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d29b0614af4e29ed">How avoid counting duplicated RecGPT-V2 paths as extra ability in π=Σgkπk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align path distributions over one candidate space, normalize the gate across actual paths, and check duplicated outputs and call costs. Copies of one policy add no information. Fixed-score proxies do not reproduce hierarchical memory and dynamic prompts merely by mixing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three paths returning the same ten popular items do not triple interest coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d29b0614af4e29ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-reco-reward-d01ebaa7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea7638de3d26e2b0">Why optimize content descriptions rather than generate user profiles online in Reco-Reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen recommender rewards audience fit while serving reads the optimized description without generating a profile. Training uses audience signals without exposing profiles online. Descriptions must remain factual despite reward pressure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Mention real pour-over attributes; do not invent them to increase affinity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea7638de3d26e2b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8f960e892ab7740">Why reward target minus non-target affinity in Reco-Reward rather than general appeal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target-only scores can favor generic popular copy. Subtracting non-target affinity encourages audience-distinguishing features. A frozen two-tower model provides a stable reward, and serving consumes descriptions without real-time user profiles. Proxy gains are not verified satisfaction.</p>
