<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Specify acidity and brewing parameters for pour-over fans rather than write &#x27;everyone loves it.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8f960e892ab7740">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-874889432bfcaf0c">Why is higher frozen Reco-Reward not equivalent to users liking copy more?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed two-tower RAS estimates affinity difference and can be exploited. Freezing stabilizes the yardstick, not its correctness. Separately verify reward, fidelity, and independent behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Stuffing audience keywords may raise model affinity while making text unreadable or misleading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-874889432bfcaf0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2287813475ac9e0">Why freeze the two towers and track non-target provenance for RAS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A drifting reward model can raise scores without better descriptions, and negative-population choice changes the subtraction. Isolate generation/selection and evaluation; test users cannot supervise training. The history-centroid proxy is not the production tower.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A weaker description can score higher if the evaluator drifts; a fixed evaluator still needs independent validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2287813475ac9e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rq-gmm-d5d0f9d6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e5696351b2fe603">Why quantize residuals repeatedly instead of clustering once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early stages encode coarse semantics and later ones encode unexplained details. Soft Gaussian posterior assignments can improve utilization, depending on clusters and features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Encode category first, then details instead of asking one code to represent everything.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e5696351b2fe603">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e9e66d9a2ee6a73">What is the trade-off between Gaussian soft assignment and hard nearest-center quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard boundaries can jump and leave centers unused. Soft posteriors combine means and pass a smoother residual to the next stage, but must connect to discrete serving. Decoupling from CTR does not guarantee click-optimal codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cooking/lifestyle clip can combine both categories before the next residual stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e9e66d9a2ee6a73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b688b0eaa9cebaca">How does separate semantic coding differ from letting CTR update the codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling preserves general semantics without guaranteeing CTR optimality. End-to-end clicks can reshape code assignments and alter stability; this is a coupling comparison, not a measured ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar items can start with similar codes, but CTR gradients might redistribute codes by popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b688b0eaa9cebaca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efde0c3f9921e8b5">What should the next RQ-GMM residual subtract?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtract the current posterior-weighted reconstruction, not a hard maximum center. Normalize probabilities and record codebook versions separately; local features proxy production multimodal inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hard subtraction after soft reconstruction changes what the next layer learns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efde0c3f9921e8b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sarm-37e57a11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc8f3fee4fd06a2a">Is a SARM semantic anchor a new item ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Offline multimodal content understanding produces it for a lightweight ranker. Identity and behavior stay separate; an anchor is not evidence of user interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stream keeps its ID while its anchor describes a changing topic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09401-sarm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc8f3fee4fd06a2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83d7cdb62eb6881b">Why generate SARM anchors offline and update lightweight ranking online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MLLMs enrich live content but are expensive per request. Offline anchors feed lightweight ranking that learns real-time user/item matching. Stale or incomplete anchors still constrain results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A ranker can use an equipment-demo anchor, but it needs refresh when the live topic changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09401-sarm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83d7cdb62eb6881b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae58a8ca3d3c68d0">Do anchors and online ID/behavior features carry the same information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Anchors describe content; IDs and behavior capture interaction and fit. Neither replaces the other, and asynchronous semantic freshness matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two camping streams can have similar descriptions but different engagement histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09401-sarm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae58a8ca3d3c68d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-90e4815c43be3546">Does local SARM generate and deploy production live anchors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens candidates test semantic injection and scoring, not private streams, real MLLMs, or clusters. Do not confuse the anchor encoder with a sparse autoencoder by the acronym SAE.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An auditable vector proxy is not a full livestream summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09401">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09401-sarm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90e4815c43be3546">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-saviorrec-24eec791" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18d2fd9fc54a1713">Why train SaviorRec&#x27;s content encoder with behavior first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic image/text similarity differs from co-click or co-purchase. SaviorEnc uses actual interactions to shape content before SID quantization. Cold start still depends on features and coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually similar products may meet different needs that behavior reveals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18d2fd9fc54a1713">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4516138032e18f25">Why freeze SID but learn behavioral residuals with zero-initialized MBA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavioral content training and quantization form stable semantic IDs. Changing IDs would disrupt historical mapping. MBA gradually adapts behavior per code, initially without changing embeddings. Stable codes can limit response to large shifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep camping IDs stable while preferences shift toward winter equipment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4516138032e18f25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c34a38d5a8bc34d">How do behavior pairs differ from content-only similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interactions adapt the space to recommendation before quantization; content similarity may only reflect surface appearance. Behavior can be exposure-biased, and a later residual does not implement encoder training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Products often chosen together can align despite looking different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c34a38d5a8bc34d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b24c0cd2199d3061">Why initialize MBA at zero, and what does bidirectional target attention read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero residuals initially preserve frozen semantics, then learn per SID. Candidate queries history and conditions historical representations; this is not access to future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate can guide matching without seeing the user&#x27;s later click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b24c0cd2199d3061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-seral-54db17e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de3a9ef7e8a1c641">Why define serendipity as relevant and unseen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Novelty alone can be irrelevant and relevance alone can repeat a feedback loop. Layered profiles and preference controls seek both before nearline candidates enter ranking. Novelty does not guarantee satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recommend unfamiliar content fitting a persistent interest, not an arbitrary obscure item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de3a9ef7e8a1c641">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bad333c1ee91eaa">Why use human and LLM CDI preferences with IPO rather than maximize logged hits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs favor past exposures. Layered profiles supply context, CDI adds judgments beyond logs, IPO aligns preference pairs with SFT constraints, and nearline caching lowers serving cost. Validate relevance and novelty separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare a suitable unseen film against a familiar one; logged hits alone favor repetition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bad333c1ee91eaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec570df74922742c">Is SERAL fully better if hit rate rises but novelty falls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Serendipity needs relevance and unseen content. Report both and their trade-off; offline proxies do not establish real user surprise or conversions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Familiar popular items can improve hits while offering fewer unseen items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec570df74922742c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-93b5c6475f26e69f">Why generate and cache nearline rather than per request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Move expensive generation off the critical path and let ranking consume cached candidates. Version profiles/cache and refresh stale candidates. Local work is not production inventory or full human CDI.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refresh after interests change instead of reusing old candidates forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93b5c6475f26e69f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sid-coord-811302bf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-540fd173d5fef393">Why keep HID and SID together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>HID memorizes head interactions while hierarchical SID shares semantics for the tail. Target gating and history alignment balance them per example, not by replacing IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Popular items use memorization; new ones rely more on semantic neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-540fd173d5fef393">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6262c1fa258fc52">Why make HID/SID fusion target-dependent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Head items have rich behavior, while tail items need semantic sharing. Target-aware gating, hierarchical fusion, and history alignment coordinate both without guaranteeing all tail gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user can receive more ID memorization for a hit film and more semantic weight for a new film.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6262c1fa258fc52">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24d82f6edd335d8c">Are hierarchical α and HID–SID gate the same axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. α mixes SID levels within an item, while the gate balances ID memory and semantics per sample. A single constant loses both distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mix coarse/fine semantics before mixing with the hash-ID branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24d82f6edd335d8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f543dce94b8b1e6">How align SID level weights and sample gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Level weights correspond to one item&#x27;s SID levels; the gate belongs to its user–target pair, not a batch constant. MovieLens proxies do not reproduce production codes or traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving A&#x27;s fine code to B misaligns semantics despite matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f543dce94b8b1e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sid-topology-a240bd6b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8465febb5f404e8f">Why audit catalog updates separately from continued training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval learns query-to-SID semantics. Remapping old items changes learned paths, and continued training may not repair arbitrary reassignments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A familiar code for shoes becomes wrong if silently remapped to bags.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8465febb5f404e8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1d31f957c262580">Why allow collisions rather than shifting old codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generator already assigns probability to old paths. Remapping sends it to other objects and short retraining may not repair it. Expand collisions while preserving addresses; test narrow-beam stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep old A pointing to its item and expand A for a newcomer rather than move the original to B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1d31f957c262580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d059fc4eff6fbca">Why doesn&#x27;t acceptable wide-beam retrieval prove remapping was harmless?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Wide search can conceal rank/path drift visible under narrow serving budgets. Separate mapping and training effects and check path stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A product found deep in a wide beam may be missing from top paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d059fc4eff6fbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e6377b739111aaa">Can old items shift when new items collide with exclusive tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Freeze all old SIDs, expand permitted collisions, and declare tail capacity with failure on exhaustion. Preserve absent old items; no silent modulo or re-encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new head item should not push old codes down one slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e6377b739111aaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sirf" data-paper-title="SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sirf-2c896048" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4bba0f8aa5a2e65c">Why train on both triggers and exemptions in SIRF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asirf">SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Safety decisions depend on exceptions as well as triggers. Synthetic rules and continued pretraining aim to cover rare combinations; thresholds manage precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A keyword need not violate policy in an explicitly exempt explanatory context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11752-sirf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4bba0f8aa5a2e65c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sirf" data-paper-title="SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-02322f33c7044fe8">Why train synthetic trigger/exemption rules and threshold one verdict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asirf">SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-tail combinations are scarce in logs. Rule graphs, rewrites, and account reasoning teach combinations during continued pretraining; one verdict saves online work. Threshold trades precision and recall. Local interactions are not production capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Frequent trades can trigger concern, but verified merchant status may exempt them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11752-sirf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02322f33c7044fe8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sirf" data-paper-title="SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f64f6bf87f503425">How does learned rule internalization differ from a runtime rules engine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asirf">SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learned models can generalize language and context but need not obey every rule exactly. Explicit engines obey coded conditions with limited coverage. Accuracy is not formal proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model may retain an old policy after the rule changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11752-sirf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f64f6bf87f503425">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sirf" data-paper-title="SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f6775ad35692318">Does the local high-precision threshold reproduce full 8B continued pretraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asirf">SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It uses trigger/exemption proxies, not private accounts, EntiGraph/MAGA generation, or large training. Select thresholds on validation and keep held-out reporting separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small classifier reaching precision target does not reproduce a safety foundation model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11752">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11752-sirf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f6775ad35692318">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ssrlive-efb93285" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e818177365a5cf26">Why use static and dynamic semantic IDs for live streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A host&#x27;s stable style and current topic change on different timescales. Combine both with interactions for viewing, commerce, and engagement; dynamic updates must be fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tech host can currently be traveling outdoors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e818177365a5cf26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-57f100938c149e13">Why retain both host-static and live-dynamic SID rather than overwrite one code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stable identity and temporary content carry different timescales. Separate codes preserve durable audience fit and current topic for multitask prediction. Dynamic IDs still have extraction and refresh lag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve a beauty host&#x27;s audience profile while indicating today&#x27;s travel-storage stream.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57f100938c149e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8142e4c5acb949a1">How does a dynamic SID differ from adding a timestamp?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It represents changing content; time alone does not identify that content. A timestamp column is not dynamic semantic generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing it is 8 pm does not reveal the product being demonstrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8142e4c5acb949a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a690900cba37e414">What can local MovieLens SSRLive establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only core static/dynamic representation and interactions, not live frames, trades, or production multitask logs. Separate task labels and snapshots from future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next rating cannot be used to construct current dynamic features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a690900cba37e414">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tagllm-3f53935e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1b41d8cb3298d8d">Why use category-specific interest manuals for TagLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different content categories need different fine-grained attributes. Manuals and multimodal reasoning structure extraction; richer labels still need user validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Food notes can encode taste and cooking method, not merely “food.”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1b41d8cb3298d8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-30c451bb8509b956">Why build category manuals before distilling multimodal tagging to a small model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Manuals define category-specific concepts that broad tags miss. A larger model supplies rich supervision and staged distillation enables cheap serving. Omitted attributes are not automatically learned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Food needs flavor/method and travel needs destination/transport rather than treating “relaxed” identically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30c451bb8509b956">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e275c4ad6f37f4ce">How does two-stage distillation differ from calling a large model per note?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It transfers expensive labeling to a smaller student, reducing serving cost subject to student capacity and coverage. Cached labels alone are not training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student must label unseen notes, not only look up old examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e275c4ad6f37f4ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-935cce9ec30720fc">Does MovieLens verify multimodal note tagging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Genre and behavior proxies test mechanisms without private images, manual generation, or production models. Teacher context H is supervision only; exclude test labels from construction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Genre prediction is not fine-grained multimodal reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-935cce9ec30720fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tokenminds-03a3a530" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-846365a6dbcec9e1">Why output both dense user vectors and SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense features remain compatible with ranking; discrete semantic tokens express multiple future interests. Neither free prose nor one user SID replaces both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain an overall vector and several prefixes for distinct interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-846365a6dbcec9e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1cf1ca5c78c492c">Why output both a dense vector and future-interest SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense output fits existing rankers but can flatten multiple interests. Item-space SID prefixes provide several actionable clusters without prose. Future-window targets are training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Represent baking and photography with separate prefixes plus a general user vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1cf1ca5c78c492c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3f9a311830fc3ad">How does a 24-hour multi-target horizon differ from next-view prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several future targets dilute accidental adjacent events, and coarse prefixes represent broader meaning. Future interactions are labels only, not encoder history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One misclick should not eclipse the day&#x27;s other interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3f9a311830fc3ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1834c322e1c99368">Does local TokenMinds run full production multi-context decoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A small GRU and SID heads preserve dual output, not Gemini scale, 15 targets, beam 40, or KV refresh serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dense and code outputs do not establish shared prefill or million-read caching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How does a new item without clicks enter a behavior-based recommender?

## Takeaway

Content semantics, collaborative identity, and user preferences are different signals. KAR adds offline generated knowledge. NoteLLM learns content vectors from co-reading and generation. Semantic IDs compress continuous content into short indexable or generatable codes. User memories and neighbors add preference evidence; feedback can train content descriptions. Align representations with recommendation objectives instead of equating linguistic similarity with preference.

## Example

A new running shoe has title and image evidence before clicks. Similar-looking shoes can appeal to different audiences. Build content representations, then align them using co-purchase or co-reading rather than treating text neighbors as the final ranking.

## Common pitfall

Better reconstruction does not ensure better recommendation. A tiny codebook collides; a large one may not learn stable collaboration. Verify generated preference descriptions rather than treating them as click labels. Cataloging a high-cost reference does not mean its model runs locally.

## Reading order

Read KAR for offline knowledge, NoteLLM for collaborative supervision, and Dual-purpose SID for short codes. All have local mechanism paths; Dual-purpose SID's small-codebook negative result illustrates quality versus compression.

1. [Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933)
2. [NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01744)
3. [Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865)

## Check your understanding

How should we interpret lower semantic-ID reconstruction MSE but worse NDCG under the same protocol?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Compression preserves content better but may preserve less collaborative signal, distinguish candidates poorly, or mismatch the decoder. Check collisions, content–behavior alignment, and retrieval separately.

</details>
